title: Tua Tagovailoa injury update: Latest news on Falcons QB being held out of training camp
description: The Falcons will have to wait a bit longer to get Tua Tagovailoa on the practice field at training camp.
fullText:
Tua Tagovailoa injury update: Latest news on Falcons QB being held out of training camp originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

When the Falcons signed Tua Tagovailoa, they gave themselves what they believed to be a good problem by entering 2026 with two starting-caliber quarterbacks on the roster.

As training camp gets underway, they instead have none.

Michael Penix Jr. hasn't been cleared for team drills, which is no surprise as he works his way back from ACL surgery, but a surprise injury to Tagovailoa has Atlanta reeling at the moment.

Here's the latest on Tagovailoa's status as camp gets underway.

MORE:Best free agents still available, from Stefon Diggs to Bobby Wagner

Tagovailoa won't practice yet after "something flared up" in his back, but head coach Kevin Stefanski said he expects the former Dolphins quarterback to return "shortly."

Stefanski says "something flared up" with Tagovailoa. "He's getting better and I expect him to be back shortly." #Falcons

— Marc Raimondi (@marcraimondi) July 29, 2026

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Tagovailoa's injury is "not considered serious" and should have him back on the practice field "next week."

Still, Tagovailoa's absence has the Falcons' quarterback room in a dire place. Atlanta also released veteran Trevor Siemian due to a non-football injury on Wednesday, so Jack Strand, undrafted out of Minnesota State-Moorhead, is taking first-team reps at the moment.

The Falcons also signed former Cowboys and Ravens QB Cooper Rush on Wednesday for additional help.

MORE:See Tony Romo's arrest video

Tagovailoa is dealing with a back injury, though the ailment is "not considered serious," Schefter reports. Stefanski said Wednesday that the quarterback's back "flared up" but didn't offer many more details.

Tagovailoa is expected back on the practice field next week, according to Schefter, with Stefanski also saying he expects Tagovailoa to return "shortly."

The Falcons will undoubtedly remain cautious with both Tagovailoa and Penix, given their injury histories, but they are hoping to have both available in some capacity in the near future.

title: Cardinals have clear Dustin May, Ryne Stanek trade deadline plan
description: St. Louis is sticking to its early-season decision.
fullText:
Cardinals have clear Dustin May, Ryne Stanek trade deadline plan originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

This season was supposed to be a rebuilding year for the St. Louis Cardinals.

Yet, on July 29, they find themselves in the NL Wild Card race. The Cardinals are 2.5 games behind the Arizona Diamondbacks for the third and final Wild Card spot.

Surprise performances up and down the roster have helped the Cardinals reach this point, but they won't be making major trades at next week's deadline.

It may be the opposite. The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal, Will Sammon and Katie Woo wrote Wednesday that the Cardinals are open to trading two of their impending free agent pitchers.

"When the St. Louis Cardinals signed Dustin May and Ryne Stanek over the offseason, they expected both veteran arms to help keep the team afloat in the first half," they wrote. "They also knew that with experienced starting and relief pitching always coveted at the deadline, they could easily flip both May and Stanek."

Reports indicate that St. Louis is sticking to that plan.

"That’s the plan for St. Louis, per multiple team sources briefed on the club’s thinking but granted anonymity to speak freely," The Athletic reported.

MORE: Giants willing to trade Heliot Ramos in big news for many MLB clubs

"Despite a surprisingly competitive first half, the Cardinals aren’t looking to deviate from president of baseball operations Chaim Bloom’s long-term outlook, which projects late 2027 or early 2028 as the team’s next competitive window."

May signed a one-year deal and has a 4.59 ERA in 20 starts. He has prior postseason experience with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Stanek also signed a one-year pact. The right-handed reliever has a 4.46 ERA in 40.1 innings but has held left-handed hitters to a .685 OPS.

title: Phillies Expect To Cut Struggling Slugger At Trade Deadline, ‘Hasn’t Been As Good’
description: Philadelphia Phillies manager Don Mattingly revealed plans to move a promising young outfielder as the trade deadline approaches.
fullText:
The Philadelphia Phillies are in the final days before the MLB trade deadline searching for answers to an offense that has stalled at an inopportune time. After another frustrating series loss, pressure continues to mount on the front office to find upgrades capable of jump-starting a lineup with postseason aspirations.

Franchise slugger Bryce Harper recently made it clear that he believes reinforcements are necessary, and the numbers back him up. Philadelphia has struggled to generate consistent production from right field, making it one of the club's most glaring weaknesses as deadline decisions approach.

FORBES | By Peter Chawaga
Shohei Ohtani’s Ex-Interpreter ‘Loved’ Dodgers Before Deception Enabled Scandal

The Phillies appear ready to move on from rookie outfielder Gabriel Rincones Jr., who has struggled to seize an everyday opportunity despite receiving extended playing time against right-handed pitching.

On Tuesday, interim manager Don Mattingly acknowledged the club's growing concern over Rincones while explaining why Bryan De La Cruz has begun taking over regular duties in right field.

“Rico’s been given a decent runway against right-handed pitching,” Mattingly said, according to The Athletic’s Matt Gelb. “Hasn’t been as good as we’d like. De La Cruz, he’s getting his hits. And I know he’s going to be solid in the outfield and all that. So I don’t feel like it’s going to be worse than what we’re seeing.”

Gelb added that Mattingly’s comments were an indication that the team expects to cut Rincones from the major-league roster as the trade deadline approaches.

“They are onto a new everyday player there, De La Cruz, who started Tuesday against a righty for the first time,” Gelb added. “He was the only one in the lineup with two hits. He has supplanted rookie Gabriel Rincones Jr., who probably won’t be in the majors after the trade deadline. Mattingly said as much before Tuesday’s game.”

FORBES | By Peter Chawaga
Cardinals Cut Starter Immediately After Brutal Outing Against Cubs

The Phillies' offensive struggles have become impossible to ignore, particularly with the trade deadline just days away.

Harper, who is mired in an extended slump, offered a direct assessment of where the club stands.

“With the Philadelphia Phillies dropping their fourth straight series since the All-Star break, Bryce Harper was blunt when asked if the team needs reinforcements as the Monday trade deadline approaches,” ESPN reported. “‘I think we need some help,’ Harper said Tuesday night after the Phillies lost 1-0 to the Marlins, their eighth defeat in 11 games since the break. They have scored one run or fewer in six of those 11 games.”

If Philadelphia acquires another outfielder before the deadline — as many around baseball expect — the roster squeeze could leave Rincones without a place on the major league club. Mattingly's comments suggest that process may already be underway, with De La Cruz earning more opportunities while the Phillies evaluate external additions.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Czech FA breaks ranks to back Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan
description: Early plans for a Uefa boycott of Fifa competitions have suffered an early blow
fullText:
The president of the Czech Football Association has backed Gianni Infantino’s controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup’s commercial rights.

After details of Infantino’s plan came to fruition on Tuesday, David Trunda told Sky News he can see the “positive impact” of the Fifa president’s plan.

For Uefa, European football’s governing body, Trunda’s comments are an early blow to their hopes of launching a member-wide boycott of Fifa competitions. In order for a boycott to take place, all 55 Uefa members would unanimously have to agree. A call to discuss the plans is scheduled for Thursday.

"I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with [FIFA president] Gianni Infantino and his team," Trunda told Sky.

"Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions.

"I was elected a little more than a year ago, and for me personally all the projects I have experienced in cooperation with FIFA have been very positive for the development of European football."

At this early stage, Trunda’s remarks are an outlier, with other high-profile football associations condemning the plans and lack of transparency. The Czech FA will discuss the proposals at an executive meeting on 11 August.

Infantino’s plan promises windfalls of $40m for Fifa member associations – of which there are 211 – who It gives members just 53 days to decide which direction they go down.

In a letter to the member associations, seen by The Independent, Infantino has promised that national federations would benefit from an increase of its ‘Fifa Forward’ funding from around $8m to $20m for the upcoming four-year cycle between 2027 and 2031 if the new FFE subsidiary is created.

Additionally, the letter states that a “one-off” payment of another $20m would be made available for member associations who vote for Infantino’s proposals on 19 September. In the letter, member associations are then warned that their funding for the 2027-2031 cycle would only stand at $10m if the vote does not pass, meaning they would miss out on $30m.

The member associations were also informed, via Fifa’s press release, that they could expect further increases in future cycles, rising to $24m by 2035 to 2038. Thrive Eternal, led Joshua Kushner, the brother of US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, are set to lead the new investment, which Fifa said could raise $4.2bn.

An English FA spokeswoman said: “We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

“Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

“When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by Fifa, we will make our views clear, and comment further.”

Uefa, ran by president Aleksander Ceferin, who does not see eye to eye with Infantino, released a strongly-worded statement on Tuesday.

"The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially,” it read. "None of us are the owners of football: it is not FIFA's to sell.”

title: Why Is Chelsea Interested In Henderson And Welbeck?
description: Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck have been linked with a summer move to Chelsea as Xabi Alonso shapes the Blues in his own image.
fullText:
Chelsea has been busy this summer. The Stamford Bridge club has broken its transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa with Marco Palestra also joining from Atalanta and Geovany Quenda coming in from Sporting CP. Chelsea has clearly altered its strategy ahead of the 2026/27 season.

This is reflected by the Blues’ interest in Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, both of whom are reportedly close to joining the Stamford Bridge outfit. Henderson is 36 while Welbeck is 35. That Chelsea is even interested in such experienced players says a lot about how the strategy has changed over the summer.

Xabi Alonso is remodelling the Chelsea team in his own image. The Spaniard is expected to recycle the approach and tactical set-up that worked so well for him as Bayer Leverkusen manager, hence the addition of a second number 10 in Rogers and a right wing back in Palestra. There is a plan in place.

Part of that plan is the addition of some much-needed experience and leadership. For a long time, Chelsea’s transfer strategy was to assemble a squad of some of the best young players in the world and develop them together. That, however, was a flawed concept, as last season’s lowly 10th place finish in the Premier League table proved.

This is where Henderson and Welbeck have something to offer. They could prove useful as squad figures, providing depth in central midfield and in the centre forward position, but Henderson and Welbeck are being targeted due to their experience at the top level. They will be mentors to some of the younger players in the squad.

“I’m sure that from today to the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of links, a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them, it’s going to be a hard task,” said Alonso when asked about the links to Henderson and Welbeck. “But for sure, we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance. We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team.”

“Balance” is the key term. Chelsea’s squad has been poorly constructed over the last few years and Alonso has been hired to point the team in the right direction again. He could use some experience in his dressing room and Henderson and Welbeck might fit the bill despite the peculiar nature of their transfers.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Done Deal: Kolo Muani to Juventus, obligation to buy €38m plus €12m bonus from PSG
description: Sky Sport Italia claim Juventus will pay €38m for Randal Kolo Muani, plus up to €12m in add-ons, on loan with obligation to buy from Paris Saint-Germain if one condition is met.ROME, ITALY – MAY...
fullText:
Sky Sport Italia claim Juventus will pay €38m for Randal Kolo Muani, plus up to €12m in add-ons, on loan with obligation to buy from Paris Saint-Germain if one condition is met.

ROME, ITALY – MAY 10: Randal Kolo Muani of Juventus celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between SS Lazio and Juventus at Stadio Olimpico on May 10, 2025 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

French sources had already suggested this afternoon that the deal was done, so that the player would fly out within 48 hours to undergo a medical and sign the contract in Turin.

Now Italian reports are giving further details on the agreement between the two clubs, which came after months of negotiations that often looked as if they were about to collapse.

BOLOGNA, ITALY – MAY 04: Randal Kolo Muani of Juventus looks on during the Serie A match between Bologna and Juventus at Stadio Renato Dall’Ara on May 04, 2025 in Bologna, Italy. (Photo by Alessandro Sabattini/Getty Images)

Everyone involved confirms this is a loan with obligation to buy at the end of the season, but Sky Sport Italia note it becomes active only if Juventus qualify for any European competition.

That is a crucial point, as the argument before was for Juve to qualify for the Champions League.

Sky Sport Italia transfer pundit Gianluca Di Marzio puts the figures specifically at a total €38m for loan and purchase option, plus up to another €12m in various add-ons.

Kolo Muani is set to sign a five-year contract worth €5.5m per season plus €1.5m in performance-related bonuses.

The figures given by transfer pundit Fabrizio Romano are more vague, stating only a package worth over €43m, while Alfredo Pedulla confirms it reaches €50m including some bonuses that are not easy to activate.

epa11889200 Juventus’ Weston McKennie (L) celebrates with his teammates after scoring the 1-0 goal during the UEFA Champions League play-offs first leg soccer match between Juventus FC and PSV Eindhoven, in Turin, Italy, 11 February 2025. EPA-EFE/ALESSANDRO DI MARCO

PSG spent €95m to buy the striker from Eintracht Frankfurt in 2023, but he never delivered on that promise, going out on loan to Juventus for six months in 2025, then last season with Tottenham Hotspur.

title: Chandler Smith addresses his NASCAR Cup Series future in 2026
description: Chandler Smith has addresses his NASCAR Cup Series future in 2026. Check out what Smith said about possibly racing in the Cup Series one day!
fullText:
Chandler Smith has been executing at a very high level in the NASCAR Truck Series during the 2026 season. With Front Row Motorsports thriving, there were rumors of Smith moving to the NASCAR Cup Series in place of Noah Gragson. However, Front Row Motorsports announced that he will not return to the organization in 2027.

So, what does Smith think about his Cup Series future? While running at NASCAR's top level is the ultimate goal, as long as Smith is behind the wheel, he will be happy. This interview was before the announcement.

“I just want the Lord’s will, whatever that means,” Smith said to NASCAR.com. “If that’s to race trucks for the rest of my life, that’s what I want to do. If the Lord obviously presents me and pushes me into an opportunity that lands in my lap and is just there and it’s pretty evident, then I want to just submit myself and be a vessel. I mean that wholeheartedly, truthfully.”

There was a time when Smith's future in NASCAR was uncertain, but it seems like he is set up for the 2027 NASCAR season. According to FOX Sports' Bob Pockrass, Smith is expected to sign with Richard Childress Racing in the NASCAR O'Reilly Series. This means Smith is one step closer to the Cup Series.

title: Brazil bans defender Gabriel until Pec returns from broken leg injury
description: Internacional's Victor Gabriel is suspended until Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec returns from a broken left leg, Brazil's sports court said.
fullText:
July 29 (UPI) -- Internacional's Victor Gabriel is suspended until Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec returns from a broken left leg injury, Brazil's sports court said.

Brazil's Superior Court of Sports Justice, or STJD, announced the ruling Tuesday. Pec fractured a tibia after Gabriel tackled him during a 2-1 win over Internacional on July 22 in Porto Alegre, Brazil.

Gabriel, who attended the STJD committee hearing for the ruling, apologized to Pec.

"I had the feeling that I would get to the ball first, and I did," Gabriel said. "Since the field was quite slippery and wet, I ended up hitting the ball and then I didn't have time to pull my leg back, and that's how this somewhat harder tackle happened, but without any intention of causing harm to my fellow professional or any malice."

The defender was given a red card for the incident. Pec's injury required surgery. Gabriel's ban, which will end when Pec returns to training, is capped at 180 days.

"I've always been a loyal guy and I've always gone onto the field to, above all, defend my club and my dream," Gabriel said. "I've always tried to be as loyal as possible to my teammates and opponents. It was a completely unfortunate incident.

"I apologized to him and offered my help. I asked him to forgive me for not having had any ill intent, and all I could do at that moment was pray for him.

"Since that night, it's been incredibly difficult for me. My whole life I've prepared for moments of happiness, and instead, it's been sleepless nights."

Internacional (5-9-6) sits at No. 16 in the Brazilian Serie A standings. Cruzeiro (7-7-6) sits at No. 11, 17 points behind first-place Palmeiras (13-2-5).

title: Schmidt to work in consultancy role at Ulster
description: Former Ireland and Australia head coach Joe Schmidt will work with Ulster in a consultancy role focused on the province's coaching pathway.
fullText:
Former Ireland and Australia head coach Joe Schmidt will work with Ulster in a consultancy role focused on the province's coaching pathway.

The position of coach development adviser is newly created for the Kiwi, and does not involve working with the senior team.

As Ulster statement said Schmidt would "support the ongoing development of coaches across the province, helping to strengthen a clear and connected coaching pathway" throughout the organisation.

The 60-year-old left his role with the Wallabies earlier this month after a win over Italy in the Nations Championship ended a run of six straight defeats.

"Ulster has a proud rugby tradition and further developing the coaching pathway in the region is something that we believe can add value," said Schmidt.

Schmidt is one of Ireland's most successful rugby coaches having led the national side between 2013 and 2019 - winning back-to-back Six Nations titles in his first two campaigns before a Grand Slam in 2018.

He was also at the helm for Ireland's first win over New Zealand and maiden triumph over the Springboks on South African soil - both in 2016.

Prior to that, Schmidt had worked as an assistant at Clermont and served as Leinster's head coach for three years, winning a pair of Heineken Cups with the latter.

Schmidt has recently been linked with a return to the RDS, with head coach Leo Cullen set to leave at the end of the 2026-27 season after more than a decade in charge.

Lowe signs for Suntory Sungoliath after Leinster exit

Ulster Rugby's general manager Rory Best, who served as Ireland captain under Schmidt, believes the appointment can be a key part of a "long-term strategy" regarding coaching development.

"Last season we introduced a dedicated focus on player development within our performance pathway. It is equally important that we prioritise the long-term development of our coaches," he said.

"Strengthening our coaching pathway is a key part of our long-term strategy.

"Joe's involvement will help us support coaches at every stage of their journey, from emerging coaches in schools and clubs through to those operating across our pathway programmes. His experience will help create a more connected and consistent coaching environment across the province."

title: Palace hold talks with ex-Arsenal defender Tomiyasu
description: Japan's Takehiro Tomiyasu, who is training with Crystal Palace, was named as a substitute in the pre-season friendly against Lens.
fullText:
Crystal Palace have held talks with Takehiro Tomiyasu over a permanent contract that would mean the defender returning to the Premier League.

Tomiyasu is training with Palace and was named as a substitute in the pre-season friendly versus Lens on Tuesday.

And the Japan international is understood to have held discussions over a permanent deal with Palace that would mean the 27-year-old joining on a free transfer.

It is understood a broad agreement on terms is in place should Palace head coach Pierre Sage decide to sign the versatile defender.

Sage is set to play with three central defenders next season and it is understood Tomiyasu, should Palace proceed, is viewed as a potential option to play on the left side of the trio.

Tomiyasu's recent career has been plagued by knee issues and, while Palace are convinced of the former Arsenal's man ability, the club want to be sure with regards to his fitness.

Upon leaving the Gunners by mutual consent last season, Tomiyasu joined Ajax, where he made eight appearances for the Dutch side towards the end of the campaign.

Palace want to strengthen their defensive options this summer with first-choice central defender Maxence Lacroix set to join Chelsea.

The Eagles have already made at least one offer for Augsburg centre-back Chrislain Matsima, with talks continuing between the two clubs over a potential 30m euro (£25.7m) deal.

Palace also have an interest in a possible loan deal for Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong, but as yet there are no indications that the Stamford Bridge club are prepared to sanction the 20-year-old's exit.

title: Harrington named as Ryder Cup vice-captain
description: Three-time major champion Padraig Harrington has been named as one of Luke Donald's vice-captains for the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor in 2027.
fullText:
Three-time major champion Padraig Harrington has been named as one of Luke Donald's vice-captains for the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor, in the Republic of Ireland, in 2027.

The 54-year-old Dubliner joins the Molinari brothers Edoardo and Francesco in Team Europe's backroom team as they bid for a third consecutive victory over USA.

Harrington played in six Ryder Cups for Team Europe and was a vice-captain on three occasions before captaining the side for the unsuccessful 2021 Ryder Cup at Whistling Straits.

"I honestly didn't think I'd ever wear the European Ryder Cup logo again, so I'm very happy to be part of it," Harrington said.

"Representing Europe has always been one of the highlights of my golfing career and to be able to do it again in this situation, especially in Ireland, is special."

Donald named Europe captain for third time

Having led Europe to a comfortable win at Rome's Marco Simone Golf Club in 2023, captain Donald stayed in post to guide them to a stunning victory on US soil at Bethpage Black, in New York, in 2025.

At Adare Manor, he could become the first captain to win three in a row and he says Harrington will form a key part of his backroom staff in his quest to make history.

"I've been around Padraig in many Ryder Cup team rooms, as a player, as a vice captain to his captaincy, and he's been a vice captain before as well," Donald said. "So he brings a wealth of experience.

"I do love the fact that there's a connection. He understands the Irish crowds and all that goes with having a Ryder Cup in Ireland. I think it's going to be very special for him.

"He's loved in Ireland with what he's achieved in the game, and that will only bring more energy to our team."

It will be the first time the competition has been held in Ireland since 2006, when Harrington was in the European team that won 18½-9½ at the K Club, County Kildare.

"You wouldn't want to miss out with it being in Ireland, so I'm very pleased," Harrington added. "I think it will be a spectacular occasion and one of the great sporting events to be played in the country. The whole of Ireland will be behind it, watching it, enjoying it and living it.

"The fans are going to be fantastic, and I think the atmosphere will be second to none."

In total, Harrington played in 25 matches across six Ryder Cups, winning 10½ points for Team Europe, while he also boasts 44 tournament victories across a glittering career.

He still plays on the DP World Tour and in major championships, most recently at The Open.

Since turning 50 in 2021, he has starred on the Champions Tour, including winning a record-equalling three US Senior Open titles.

title: Rayo Vallecano to move stadium over Legionnaires risk
description: La Liga side Rayo Vallecano are barred from playing at their home stadium just weeks before the new season over the risk of supporters contracting Legionnaires' disease.
fullText:
La Liga side Rayo Vallecano have been barred indefinitely from playing at their home stadium less than three weeks before the start of the new season because of the risk of supporters contracting Legionnaires' disease.

Rayo rent the Estadio de Vallecas from the regional government of Madrid but have had their licence to host matches suspended after an audit highlighted serious health and safety issues.

A regional government report cited the risk of Legionnaires' disease outbreaks or fires due to the accumulation of refuse and debris inside the stadium, as well as electrical faults.

To date, no alternative venue for home games has been confirmed.

Legionnaires' disease is a serious lung infection caused by inhaling droplets of water containing bacteria.

Mariano ⁠de Paco, Madrid's regional head of sport, culture and tourism, told reporters on Tuesday the club had not complied with requests to carry out maintenance and provide proof of water quality.

"We've tried to get this back on track but we've reached a point of no return - the lack of maintenance has been certified," he said.

"The club wasn't complying so authorities had ​to take action. What has happened is intolerable."

De Paco confirmed urgent work on the stadium will begin immediately and could take between two and six months to complete.

He added he has been unable to contact Rayo president Raul Martin Presa, who has long been criticised by the club's fans and players for the poor upkeep of facilities and a failure to modernise the club.

Last season, the Spanish football association published a letter written by Rayo's players that described the Vallecas pitch as "unplayable" and noted a lack of hot water in the showers and inadequate cleaning.

They began last season without being able to use their own training ground because of mould but were able to reach the final of the Uefa Conference League which they lost 1-0 to Crystal Palace.

Supporters regularly have to queue for hours to purchase match tickets at the stadium's small box office as Rayo is the only top-flight Spanish club without a ticketing website.

Last month the regional government proposed a two-year stadium renovation plan that would include a new stand to increase capacity to 18,500.

In February, Rayo were forced to play a home match against Atletico Madrid at the home of Madrid neighbours Leganes because of poor pitch conditions at Vallecas.

Rayo launched their season ticket renewal campaign last week with an ​average price increase of 15% for adults.

A clause in the renewal terms appears to anticipate the closure of the stadium as it says in the event matches cannot be played in Vallecas then season ticket holders will be given seats "in the most ​similar location possible" at the chosen alternative venue.

Rayo's first home game of the season is against Alaves and is scheduled for Thursday, 20 August.

title: Mooney stars as Rockets cruise to win against Fire
description: Trent Rockets register their second win in The Hundred women's competition by cruising to an eight-wicket victory against Welsh Fire in Cardiff.
fullText:
The Hundred women's competition, Sophia Gardens

Welsh Fire 129-3 (100 balls): Devine 38 (25); Phillips 2-17

Trent Rockets 132-2 (83 balls): Mooney 57 (35); Arlott 1-15

Trent Rockets won by eight wickets

Trent Rockets registered their second win in The Hundred women's competition by cruising to an eight-wicket victory against Welsh Fire in Cardiff.

Having restricted Fire to 129-3, Rockets made light work of the chase, with Beth Mooney setting the tone with a superb half-century at the top of the order.

Opening alongside Sophia Dunkley, the Australian wicketkeeper-batter did most of the damage in a first-wicket partnership of 73 that put Rockets firmly in control.

Dunkley departed after picking out Heather Graham in the deep but by then, the visitors only needed 57 more to win from 60 balls.

Joined by Nat Sciver-Brunt in the middle, Mooney brought up her 50 from just 27 balls before falling for 57.

But the England captain's unbeaten 37 - in her first game of the campaign after missing the first two - ensured Rockets overhauled the target with 17 balls to spare.

Sent out to bat first, Fire had made a slow start, losing openers Georgia Voll and Ella McCaughan early to slip to 28-2 after 41 balls.

The home side were 41-2 at the halfway stage of their innings but Sophie Devine and Freya Kemp accelerated in the second half to steer Fire to a respectable total.

Devine led the recovery with a knock of 38 from 25 balls that included two fours and two sixes, while Kemp remained unbeaten on 36 from 29 deliveries with support from Georgia Wareham, who added 19 from just 10 balls.

Southern Brave face Birmingham Phoenix in Southampton on Thursday.

In the women's competition, the home side, who sit at the top of the table, will be aiming for a fourth win from as many matches, while Phoenix are yet to win after two games. They meet at 15:00 BST.

Brave's men, meanwhile, will be eyeing their first win of the season in the match that follows at 18.30.

title: Saltburn concede match over 'finger-clicking' claim
description: Saltburn Cricket Club were placed under investigation by the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League earlier this week.
fullText:
Following the furore surrounding Saltburn Cricket Club amid an alleged cheating scandal, the club's second team were due to return to action on Wednesday evening.

But that match, a cup game against Marton's second team, has now been cancelled.

Saltburn have conceded the fixture, with BBC Sport being told Saltburn were unable to get a team together due to the "holiday season".

Earlier on Wednesday morning, the match had been scheduled to go ahead as planned but was later cancelled.

On Monday evening, the North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League placed the club under investigation following a complaint made after their second XI victory over Norton in Division 2. Footage of the match went viral on social media.

At the heart of the controversy is Saltburn batter Brian Devine, who is alleged to have clicked his finger at the exact moment the ball passed Norton batter Noman Shabir's bat and the ball was caught by wicketkeeper Josh Bowes. Following an appeal to the umpire, the wicket was given.

Since that video was posted, other videos involving Saltburn and Devine from previous matches have also been posted alleging similar incidents.

The original video has received over seven and a half million views on X and Devine has been dubbed as 'Clicky Ponting' on social media. The BBC has approached Devine for comment.

A meeting on Tuesday night was held between Saltburn, the league and legal representatives though any outcomes from that meeting are yet to be made public.

The league, Saltburn, Norton and the England and Wales Cricket Board have all declined to comment on the incident.

Saltburn's second team were due to play against Marton in a first-round match in the Division Two Hundred competition, a 100-ball-per-side format akin to The Hundred.

title: Season to end in Europe if war continues - F1 boss
description: Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali says the 2026 championship will end in Europe if the conflict in the Middle East makes it impossible to hold the season-closing races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
fullText:
Formula 1 president Stefano Domenicali says the 2026 championship will end in Europe if the conflict in the Middle East makes it impossible to hold the season-closing races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Domenicali said on a call with F1 media that a final decision would be made by the "middle of September".

"For us today, the races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are confirmed," Domenicali said. "By the way, they are already sold out. That is an incredible sign of how much the sport is bigger than the problem that our world is living.

"But of course, if the situation will not be cleared the way that we believe it should be, before the middle of September we will take the decision.

"If this will not be possible, the end of the season will be in Europe, because we cannot go in other places."

The 61-year-old did not elaborate on where the final race would be held if Qatar and Abu Dhabi have to be called off, but the strong front-runner is the Imola circuit in Italy.

F1 has already been forced to cancel the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia races, which were scheduled for April, as a result of the US-Israel war with Iran.

The sport announced on Sunday that Malaysia would step in hold a race in September on behalf of Bahrain.

Although that event takes F1 to the 21 grands prix needed to satisfy various commercial contracts, Domenicali is determined for there to be another race after the Las Vegas Grand Prix on 21 November.

Domenicali said: "There was a possibility of having two races in Las Vegas, but we don't want to ruin, let me put it this way, a jewel that is growing by undervaluing what we are doing there.

"And of course, we don't have to forget that in that period of the year, we are fighting in the US against the NFL.

"That is a major sport that is, I don't want to say detracting, but a lot of fans are watching that. So we need to avoid any kind of situation that would put us in front of something that, of course, is still quite big in the US."

Next year, the opening race is set to revert to Bahrain after two years in Australia as a result of the timing of the Muslim holy month of Ramadan.

Domenicali said contingency plans were in place should the war still be ongoing, he added.

"So far, the calendar that will be presented, let's say in autumn, will be as a sort of a normal plan," Domenicali said.

"But in case the situation in the Middle East will be not solved, we have options, different plan. And the trigger for that, of course, is at the end of the year."

He said these alternative plans would "accommodate the fact that we will keep, in any case, the target of 24 countries also for next year".

Five things we've learned from first half of F1 season

Listen to Back at Base on BBC Sounds

This year's new engines, with a nominal 50-50 split between internal combustion and electrical power, have been criticised by drivers for reducing their ability to drive on the limit.

This is caused by the need to constantly recharge the batteries, which is reducing the challenge of fast corners by turning them into what two-time champion Fernando Alonso has called "charging stations".

But Domenicali said: "There is a lot of action on the track. People are loving it. They are focused on what is happening on the track.

"They don't understand our technology, division of 'clipping', or whatever it is, because it's too technical for the wider base that we have. Therefore, the effect on the track has been widely super positive about the fans."

He acknowledged steps taken to reduce the effect of energy recovery on driving over the next two seasons as "the right thing for the sport".

And he admitted he had asked drivers to be "constructive" in their comments after outspoken remarks from Max Verstappen, Lando Norris and others.

"We are not here to put tape on the mouth of anyone," Domenicali said. "The beauty of motorsport is that everyone can have an opinion, but the opinion is an opinion. I prefer to discuss things in that respect in four walls to find solutions."

The new engines have presented an opportunity for Mohammed Ben Sulayem, the president of F1's governing body the FIA, to push his plan for a return to naturally aspirated V8 engines for the next set of engine rules in 2030 or 2031.

Ben Sulayem has threatened to impose his wishes unilaterally for 2031, because at that point the FIA is free to do what it likes as the teams' contracts all expire in 2030.

But Domenicali said the sport was on track to have an outline plan for the next engine rules by the end of this year.

"The main target of the future regulation is to keep things as simple as possible, to bring F1 to a lighter class [of car weight], with a sustainable fuel, with, of course, electrification, and around this give the chance to the drivers, above all, in a certain mode, to push as hard as they can," he said.

"I do believe that within the end of this year, we're going to be in a position to have a package ready to be discussed.

"Because there are two options.

"If we wait for the end of the cycle to be finished, in 2031, there's nothing that prevents the FIA to present a totally different regulation. And, of course, if the teams want to be part of it, they can, otherwise, no. I'm exaggerating, but you understand the principle.

"If there is a consensus on what we are doing, to anticipate it, there is the need to find the governance in place with the teams, with the manufacturers.

"There are a lot of good talks going ahead now. There is a lot of, as you can imagine, different angles that everyone is pushing for different reasons, but within the end of the year, we're going to be in a position to have the right package for the future."

Most of the engine manufacturers are open to the idea of a V8 architecture, but both Mercedes and Audi want turbochargers to remain and talks are said to be moving in that direction.

It is also expected that the engines will retain a relatively significant proportion of electrical power to ensure they are road-relevant.

title: Trump broke his promise to lower — and eliminate — the national debt. A top investor thinks he’s the ‘worst-spending president in history’
description: "The number one job of the President is to get the deficit under control,” Jason Calacanis wrote in a post on X.
fullText:
The U.S. national debt reached its highest ever level of $39.5 trillion in June, a 37% increase from its pre-pandemic levels, and one top VC is putting the blame squarely on President Donald Trump.

In total, the government now owes the equivalent of $113,000 per person, according to USAFacts, a nonprofit civic initiative cofounded by former Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer which aggregates and analyzes government data.

What is the current size of U.S. national debt?

What are long-term consequences of rising national debt?

How much debt did Trump add during presidency?

How does national debt affect everyday Americans' borrowing?

These eye-popping numbers are a problem for tech entrepreneur and All-In Podcast cohost Jason Calacanis, who called out President Trump for contributing to the problem in a post on X last week.

"President Trump has become the worst-spending President in our history, adding ~$2.2-$2.3 T to the national debt in each of his first two years and in his second term," Calacanis claimed in his post.

To be sure, data from Congress' Joint Economic Committee shows the national debt actually increased $2.25 trillion during the first year of President Trump's second term—a sum which climbed to $3.16 trillion through July. Still, Trump may not have approved of all the funding which raised the debt levels, some of which may have been allocated and approved before he took office. During his first term, Trump added $2.2 trillion of debt in his first two years, according to a 2024 report by the nonpartisan Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget.

Still, Calcanis also argued Trump has reneged on a key campaign promise to make the government more fiscally responsible.

"President Trump promised not to add to the national debt during his presidential campaign — and, in fact, that he would pay it down," he wrote. "He has failed badly on both counts."

In 2016, Trump said he would eliminate the country's debt, which at the time stood at $19 trillion, "over a period of eight years." It has more than doubled instead. Last year, he supported the idea of using 20% of the savings from the Elon Musk-led budget slashing initiative DOGE to pay down the debt.

White House spokesperson Kush Desai said in a statement to Fortune that Trump is the first president to seriously take on waste, fraud, and abuse in the federal government.

"The Trump administration has already secured billions in discretionary spending savings for the American people by right-sizing the federal workforce to its lowest level since the 1960s, slashing wasteful programs, and implementing other commonsense reforms. As the President's growth and savings agenda continues taking effect, America's debt-to-GDP ratio is set to trend in the right direction," Desai wrote in the statement.

title: Why am I getting a second Social Security check this month?
description: Why are you getting two Social Security checks this July?
fullText:
Supplemental Security Income recipients in Philadelphia can expect a second check this month, but that doesn't mean they're getting extra money.

The seemingly double payout is just a result of the Social Security Administration payment calendar.

While recipients typically get their checks on the first of the month, alterations are made when payment day falls on a weekend or holiday, and this month is no exception.

According to the SSA, 90,405 people in Philadelphia received SSI benefits, as of June 2026.

Technically, yes, there will be two Supplemental Security Income payouts during the month, but that's not extra money.

The SSI Aug. 1 payment will payout on July 31 because August begins on a weekend, according to the 2026 SSA calendar.

Based on the SSA payment calendar, SSI recipients can expect this calendar quirk to happen at least twice more.

In October, recipients will get their normal payment on the first, as well as November's payment on Friday, Oct. 30.

And in December, recipients will get their payment on the first as well as their January 2027 payment on Thursday, Dec. 31 since Jan. 1 is a holiday.

Kaitlyn McCormick is a Philadelphia-based reporter writing all things trending, breaking and city-related for USA TODAY's Philadelphia Metro Connect Team.

title: US thwarts an Iranian missile attack and launches strikes with Saudi Arabia against militias in Iraq
description: The U.S. military said Tuesday that it knocked down an Iranian missile barrage and worked with Saudi Arabia's forces to strike sites in Iraq that Tehran-backed militias have used to launch attacks in ...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. military said Tuesday that it knocked down an Iranian missile barrage and worked with Saudi Arabia's forces to strike sites in Iraq that Tehran-backed militias have used to launch attacks in recent days, shattering a brief pause in fighting.

All Iranian missiles launched against American forces in the Middle East were intercepted, U.S. Central Command said, adding that they "remain vigilant and at a high state of readiness." In announcing the strikes in Iraq, the U.S. warned that further attacks on American troops or Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure risked additional action.

The United States and Iran had experienced a period of calm, during which neither announced attacks for days following weeks of escalation over the strategic Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf waterway and narrow chokepoint through which 20% of the world's traded oil normally flows.

There was no immediate comment from Tehran on the U.S. military statement or the strikes.

The fighting flared at the end of a month packed with multiple pressure points on President Donald Trump. In recent weeks, four U.S. troops died during the fighting, while the Pentagon asked an increasingly skeptical Congress for money to cover the conflict's ballooning costs.

High gasoline prices tied to the choked-off Strait of Hormuz are contributing to fears that Republicans are vulnerable in November's midterm elections. The U.S. House narrowly passed a resolution to halt military action in Iran last week, sending another warning to Trump that reflects the war's unpopularity with many Americans.

Trump has repeatedly retreated from threats to knock out bridges, power plants and other infrastructure but he told Fox News Channel earlier Tuesday that Iran knows he'll "finish the job" if its leaders don't make a deal to end the war.

Iran launched its ballistic missile attack before American and Saudi forces carried out strikes in Iraq, according to a U.S. official, who stressed that the two attacks were not connected. The official spoke on condition of anonymity to detail sensitive military operations.

"U.S. and Saudi fighter aircraft struck multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours," U.S. Central Command said, using an acronym for Iran's paramilitary Revolutionary Guard.

It said the Revolutionary Guard "and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further U.S. military response."

The Saudi Defense Ministry acknowledged the strikes in a post on social media, warning that "the Kingdom emphasizes that it does not seek escalation but will respond to any aggression it faces."

Saudi Arabia said Tuesday that it shot down drones fired by Iran-backed militias in Iraq for a second day, while Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen claimed to have forced a Saudi oil tanker to turn around as part of their self-styled blockade of the kingdom.

The kingdom's Defense Ministry said air defenses intercepted and destroyed several drones that had tried to target petroleum facilities in the nation's eastern region.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered security agencies to investigate after the Saudis alleged a similar attack on Monday. The Iraqi military said the country is committed to "preventing Iraqi territory from being used as a route or launching point for any attack targeting brotherly or friendly countries."

The Iraqi militias have denied any role in the drone attacks. The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, an umbrella group of Iran-backed armed groups, called the Saudi claims "fabrications" and implied that Monday's attacks were carried out by the Houthis, who had themselves claimed to have attacked Saudi oil facilities.

The Houthis claimed to have fired missiles at the Saudi oil tanker NCC Ghazal, forcing it to turn back. Last week, they announced a blockade of Saudi shipping, putting another key Middle Eastern waterway — through the Bab el-Mandeb strait leading to the Red Sea — at risk.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Center said a tanker reported hearing explosions while traveling in the southern Red Sea. It did not name the tanker but said the crew and vessel were safe.

The rebels fired on at least one Saudi tanker in the Red Sea last week.

Iran and the U.S. had paused their fighting over the weekend, though tensions remained high even as officials said mediators achieved progress in getting the two sides back to negotiations.

Iran said earlier Tuesday that U.S. strikes during an earlier period of escalation destroyed an airport and a marine control tower, and caused damage to 12 bridges and two tunnels, among other infrastructure.

Iran had effectively closed the strait when the war began by firing at freighters and tankers off its coast or threatening them. Following the signing of an interim ceasefire deal in June, a battle for control over the strait erupted.

Iran demanded that ships use a route near its coastline and said it can potentially charge fees. Ships were increasingly navigating a southern route along the coast of Oman under a U.S. overwatch operation when Iran attacked some vessels.

The new strikes came on the same day Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Trump at the White House for the first time since the two launched the war against Iran on Feb. 28. Israel has been notably absent from the recent fighting with the Islamic Republic.

Netanyahu said it was an "excellent" meeting, and Trump called it "very good," noting that "many important subjects were discussed."

Meanwhile, the U.S. ability to intercept Iran's incoming strikes has become an increasingly salient issue as lawmakers, members of the military and experts raise concerns over the nation's diminishing stockpiles of missile interceptors.

Sean Parnell, the Pentagon's chief spokesperson, pushed back on those concerns, saying the military "has everything it needs to execute at the time and place of the president's choosing."

title: Ukrainian drones strike across Russia, hitting refineries, Wildberries warehouse
description: July 29 (Reuters) - Ukrainian drones hit oil refineries and logistics facilities in the Russian cities of Perm, Ryazan and Taganrog, as well as the Crimean peninsula overnight, with the country's top
fullText:
July 29 (Reuters) - Ukrainian drones hit oil refineries and logistics facilities in the Russian cities of Perm, Ryazan and Taganrog, as well as the Crimean peninsula overnight, with the country's top online retailer Wildberries evacuating ‌its Ryazan warehouse.

While Ukraine's air defences are running low on interceptors like Patriot missiles, leaving it more exposed to ‌Russian strikes, its own deep-strike drone production has outpaced Russia's, enabling it to hit Russian oil refineries and infrastructure and cause fuel shortages across its ​11 time zones.

Drone strikes have damaged at least seven Wildberries warehouses in the past few days, destroying around 10% of the company's storage capacity and inflicting losses on tens of thousands of small businesses that sell goods and services via the platform, according to the company and local authorities.

In a statement, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said his forces had struck oil refineries in Perm and Ryazan, a ‌logistics centre in Ryazan, an export terminal ⁠and military plant in the Rostov region, as well as a naval base in Crimea.

Local Russian officials confirmed the strikes.

RYAZAN WILDBERRIES WAREHOUSE ABLAZE

In Ryazan, south of Moscow and around 500 km (310 miles) from ⁠Ukrainian-held territory, Governor Pavel Malkov said industrial sites had caught fire and six people were seeking medical help. Wildberries said its Ryazan site had been evacuated and had stopped accepting deliveries of goods. Video footage on social media, verified by Reuters, showed a large blaze at ​Wildberries' ​Ryazan facility.

Russian business daily Kommersant reported on Wednesday that Wildberries is ​seeking 100,000 square metres of storage space in neighbouring ‌Kazakhstan to protect its goods from Ukrainian strikes.

In the Urals city of Perm, around 1,600 km from Ukrainian-held territory, Governor Dmitry Makhonin said Ukrainian drones had hit an industrial facility but caused no casualties. He did not name the facility.

In the southern Rostov region, Governor Yuri Slyusar said that a woman was killed and a man injured after missile debris hit an apartment building in the port city of Taganrog on the Sea of Azov, home to various industrial facilities and a grain terminal.

On ‌the Crimean peninsula, seized from Ukraine by Russia in 2014, Moscow-backed governor ​Sergei Aksyonov said that two people had been killed and five injured in ​overnight drone strikes.

On the Ukrainian side of the front ​line, a man was killed and another three people injured in a Russian drone attack on ‌the city of Kherson, local authorities said on Telegram.

Russia's ​Defence Ministry said its drones ​hit two vessels carrying weapons and military equipment east of the Ukrainian port of Odesa.

Ukraine and Russia have stepped up strikes on vessels in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov in recent weeks, leading to a fall in ​oil and grain supplies in the region.

title: Jamie Dimon says his stockbroker father taught him to invest with a ‘brutally hard’ childhood game
description: The JPMorgan Chase CEO spent his childhood playing stock market simulation games and reading non-fiction economics books.
fullText:
Like legendary investor Warren Buffett, JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon's finance career started in childhood. But in an unusually hands-on fashion, Dimon spent hours playing investment simulation games with his father.

"He would give me an industry you might know something about, like a restaurant," Dimon said on a recent episode of The Master Investor Podcast with Wilfred Frost. "And say, 'Okay, look at this. Look at the history. Read the annual report. Study the industry if you want. What would you pay for the stock?"

That early training would prove foundational. Dimon, now 70, has run JPMorgan Chase for nearly two decades and built it into the largest bank in the U.S.—but the instinct for pricing a business started at his father's side, long before business school.

A Wall Street stockbroker, Dimon's father, Theodore, encouraged all three of his sons to learn more about the markets, but only Jamie leaned in. While his brothers showed little interest, Dimon gravitated toward big business bets and used the simulation games to learn the fundamentals of stock picking and decision making.

"It is brutally hard," Dimon said. "Then you learn the 'why.'"

"I read Graham and Dodd in high school—I was a nerd," Dimon said. "I read all of Freud's books. I always would be taking this stuff in."

At 14 years old, Dimon bought his first stock in 1970 with guidance from his father, and never looked back.  He went on to graduate from Tufts University before earning an MBA from Harvard Business School. After graduation, Dimon landed his first Wall Street role as an assistant to then-American Express president Sanford "Sandy" Weill.

"My first goal was to learn something and not say anything until I could add some value," a 28-year-old Dimon told Fortune in a 1984 profile.

The apprenticeship under Weill became Dimon's real business school. Dimon had joined Weill as his assistant at American Express in 1982, and when the two left to take over consumer lender Commercial Credit in 1986, Dimon became CFO at just 30 years old. Under Weill's mentorship, Dimon learned the inner workings of banking, a foundation that paved the way for more senior positions at Citigroup and Bank One, the latter of which merged with JPMorgan Chase in 2004. Two years later, in 2006, Dimon became the CEO of JPMorgan Chase.

Today, Dimon is one of the only remaining Wall Street CEOs still in place from the 2008 financial crisis. He led JPMorgan for nearly two decades, making him an outlier among his peers, whose tenures typically lasted under a decade, according to Esgauge data. The bank is now the largest bank in the U.S., and ranked No. 12 on the Fortune 500 list and No. 19 on the Global 500.

title: Blazes burning with the intensity of ‘atomic bombs’: Europe enters a new era of mega fires
description: The vast blazes ripping through southwestern France burned so intensely they created a powerful, fire-generated thunderstorm — and it’s just one sign that Europe is entering a new fire era, experts sa...
fullText:
The vast blazes ripping through southwestern France burned so intensely they created a powerful, fire-generated thunderstorm. This rare phenomenon is sometimes seen in the kinds of megafires that afflict the US and Canada, but was unprecedented in France, until now — and it's just one sign that Europe is entering a new fire era, experts say.

Europe has always had wildfires, but they are becoming increasingly extreme as the climate crisis tightens its grip. Firefighters in France and Spain are currently trying to tame blazes more ferocious and more erratic than anything they've tackled before.

This follows from Europe's record-breaking fire season last year, with experts saying the continent is joining a long list of regions — from Siberia to the Amazon — which now endure back-to-back extreme fire seasons.

"We have entered an era of fires that cannot be extinguished," said Víctor Resco de Dios, lecturer of forestry engineering and global change at the University of Lleida in Spain. "These are fires that burn with the intensity of several atomic bombs."

🔥 CNN Weather app brings you climate news and local weather

Wildfires in France have now scorched more than 116,000 hectares (roughly 290,000 acres), making them the largest on record for the country, and there are still months of wildfire season left.

"The situation we face today is the hardest we've ever recorded, the hardest since the Second World War," French President Emmanuel Macron said Monday on a visit to Bordeaux. He called the fires "totally unprecedented."

One of the most visceral examples of this was the appearance of fire clouds, or "pyrocumulonimbus," which formed over the weekend in the Gironde region, near Bordeaux, according to fire authorities.

Fire clouds emerge when particularly intense wildfires generate a plume of extreme heat, which rises rapidly into the cooler air above and condenses into towering thunderstorm clouds. These can create their own wind, rain and lightning and transform blazes into erratic and unpredictable self-feeding firestorms.

The phenomenon is well documented in Australia, Canada and the US — the Los Angeles fires in 2025 produced a rare tornado, or firenado — but they are not at all common in Europe.

The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts said it could not yet say for certain this was France's first pyrocumulonimbus. "However, if confirmed, its development would highlight the exceptional intensity of the current fire and the extraordinary atmospheric conditions under which it is burning," said Francesca Di Giuseppe, fire forecast coordinator at the ECMWF.

The scale of the fires is also remarkable, experts said. They have scorched huge tracts of land across France and Spain, both of which have requested EU assistance. "A synchronized, multinational wildfire crisis is rare in Europe," said Stefan Doerr, director of the Centre for Wildfire Research at Swansea University in Wales.

The fires are raging near major cities, including one which has torn through the mountainous province of Avila, west of the Spanish capital Madrid, and is now the country's largest on record, authorities have said.

"What is uncommon is the current number of destructive wildfires: fires that spread rapidly, overwhelm fire brigades and force communities to evacuate," said Guillermo Rein, professor of fire science at Imperial College London. More than 300,000 people have been evacuated across the two countries so far.

Complete suppression of fires of this magnitude is almost impossible until the fuel runs out or persistent rain arrives, no matter how many firefighting resources are mobilized, experts say.

"In Australia, parts of the US and Canada, there is a general expectation and acceptance of out-of-control wildfires," said Swansea University's Doerr. "In Europe there is still a widely held notion that such fires can be entirely prevented."

Each wildfire is complex and unique and affected by many factors, including land management, terrain and firefighting resources. But extreme weather, made worse by climate change, has been a key driver of Europe's fires, scientists say.

Global warming is bringing stronger swings between wet and dry extremes. It's a "whiplash effect," said Matthew Jones, an independent research fellow at the School of Environmental Sciences at the University of East Anglia in England.

Last winter was unusually wet in France and Spain, leading a surge in vegetation growth. Then the weather flipped. Since May, Western Europe has been roiled by a succession of brutal heat waves, which parched the landscape. This heat provided "the 'crack of the whip' in the whiplash effect, turning that dense vegetation into highly combustible fuel," Jones said.

As France and Spain brace for their fourth heat wave of the summer, there are fears it may exacerbate and already dangerous situation.

Extinguishing the current fires completely may take months, authorities have said, but their impacts will linger long after that.

The hazardous, smoke-filled skies they produce are harmful to health. Pollution from wildfires is estimated to cause more than 100,000 deaths globally every year.

There's also the damage to economies. These fires are raging near major European cities, affecting tourist hotspots, wine-growing regions and vital defense hubs.

More than that, they may change people's relationship with the land they live on, now they find themselves under the constant threat of uncontrollable fires.

Into the future, scientists say we should expect fires — in Europe as elsewhere — to become more frequent and more extreme as long as humans continue to burn fossil fuels and push up temperatures.

"It's difficult to predict how far things might go," said Resco de Dios, "we will soon be unable to rule out Dantean scenarios like those seen in California or Australia, with fires or fire complexes reaching hundreds of thousands of hectares or even a million hectares."

title: Jackson accused of 'trying to buy' election after $87 million promise
description: Republican gubernatorial candidate Rick Jackson vows another $87 million for ad buys. Opponents accuse him of buying the election.
fullText:
In a meteoric rise from political unknown to the Republican gubernatorial candidate in Georgia, Rick Jackson has used his vast personal wealth to help spread his message.

The healthcare CEO and reported self-made billionaire entered Georgia's governor's race late in the game, announcing his candidacy in February after President Trump had already endorsed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones for the state's top seat.

He quickly rose in the polls, making what could have been a relatively easy campaign for Jones into a two-person race. Jackson and Jones made it to a primary runoff, and in the final days Jackson pulled ahead, ultimately earning the nomination in June.

Jackson is a self-funded candidate, a key part of his political message that he can't be bought and isn't beholden to outside special interests. After investing more than an estimated $100 million on the campaign so far, his team is continuing to funnel his personal wealth into the bank for his race.

Jackson is facing former Democratic mayor of Atlanta Keisha Lance Bottoms in the general election on Nov. 3.

As the country reaches fewer than 100 days before the general election, Jackson's team announced he was putting another $87 million into ads to spread his campaign message across the state. It's the largest buy so far in the race.

"This is the largest general election buy of this race, and it reflects exactly how seriously we take the job of earning every vote in every one of Georgia's 159 counties," campaign spokesperson Garrison Douglas told Atlanta News First. "Rick Jackson has spent this campaign showing up in places candidates usually skip, and this buy makes sure all 11 million Georgians hear the same thing the people in those rooms have heard, which is that he is running to fight for them."

Jackson's ads in the past few months have ranged from focusing on his upbringing in the foster care system to telling immigrants they would end up "deported or departed" if he became governor.

More recently, he's focused his ad buys on attacking Bottoms and her record in Atlanta. Quotes from Bottoms play over the sounds of sirens and images of cars and buildings on fire in one ad titled "Never Again" posted in June.

He's also likely to start using clips from the recent visit from President Trump in his new round of ads, as he becomes the new Trump-endorsed candidate.

Trump gave a speech in Marietta last week intended to focus on the rollout of Trump Accounts. But, he spent much of his time on other topics like Iran and attacking Senator Jon Ossoff. He also took the opportunity to welcome Jackson on stage, marking the first public appearance between the two businessmen-turned-politicians. Jackson has often compared himself to Trump, and said on stage that ongoing affordability issues were a business problem, not a political one.

He also vowed to use his wealth once again as it relates to Trump Accounts. Jackson said he would push Georgia legislators to match the $1,000 federal contribution to the investment accounts for children, and that if they didn't support it, he would personally donate the money. There are more than 120,000 children born in Georgia each year, all of whom will now be eligible for the accounts, meaning it could cost millions to match the investments.

During the primary campaign, Jones repeatedly accused Jackson of thinking he could buy his way to the governor's seat. After the latest ad vow, Bottoms is taking on the same message.

"Rick Jackson is everywhere spending over $100 million trying to buy our vote," one Jones ad said. "But Georgia is not for sale."

.@RickJacksonGA has spent over $100 million trying to do one thing: buy your vote. It's time we tell him, Georgia's not for sale, y'all. #gapol pic.twitter.com/fZqmoQFNRk

— Burt Jones (@burtjonesforga) June 11, 2026

In a statement from TaNisha Cameron, Bottoms' campaign spokesperson, the Bottoms camp pointed out that at least some of Jackson's wealth came from state contracts for health care services through Jackson's company, Jackson Healthcare. The company has an annual revenue over $3 billion, according to Forbes.

"Rick Jackson made a billion dollars off of taxpayer-funded contracts with the state for health care services, even while rural hospitals closed and Georgians lost health care coverage, and now he's trying to buy this election," Cameron said. "Jackson's in this for himself and to serve Donald Trump, and Keisha's the only candidate in this race who will stand up for Georgians."

Bottoms echoed this message during a recent "Mandate" town hall focused on Black male voters.

"I'm not mad about his money. But I am mad about the way that he is manipulating the narrative with his money," Bottoms said. "And for everybody who is taking money from him, God bless you. A good friend of mine who's probably in this room often reminds me: If you can be bought, you can be sold."

Bottoms also addressed the recent messaging surrounding Toast on Lenox, a Black-owned Atlanta restaurant that recently hosted a Jackson visit. Jackson accused Bottoms of cancelling the restaurant for speaking with Jackson, while Bottoms called the visit performative.

"The theatrics are nice, but what is the real worth? What are you actually doing? What do your policies stand for? I'm talking about the policies; it's not that I'm not making these stops, but I make these stops as part of my everyday life. I live in southwest Atlanta, and I am surrounded by Black businesses, so I don't have a camera crew with me every time I walk into one," Bottoms said at the town hall.

Irene Wright covers Georgia politics as the Atlanta Connect reporter with USA TODAY's Deep South Connect team. Find her on X @IreneEWright or email her at ismith@usatodayco.com.

title: Ebay and ex-executives to pay $55.7m to couple sent cockroaches in harassment campaign
description:

Ebay and three former top executives have agreed to pay $55.7m to resolve a lawsuit by a Massachusetts couple who fell victim ⁠to a bizarre stalking and ⁠harassment campaign carried out ​by several of its employees in retaliation for their coverage of the e-commerce company in a newsletter they publish.
David and Ina Steiner announced the settlement late on Monday, bringing an end to a ⁠case they filed in 2021 in Boston federal court after several former eBay employees were prosecuted for targeting them in a cyberstalking campaign that involved sending the couple cockroaches, fly larvae and a bloody Halloween pig mask.

fullText:
Bloggers David and Ina Steiner were stalked by eBay executives over their critical coverage of the company

Ebay and three former top executives have agreed to pay $55.7m to resolve a lawsuit by a Massachusetts couple who fell victim ⁠to a bizarre stalking and ⁠harassment campaign carried out ​by several of its employees in retaliation for their coverage of the e-commerce company in a newsletter they publish.

David and Ina Steiner announced the settlement late on Monday, bringing an end to a ⁠case they filed in 2021 in Boston federal court after several former eBay employees were prosecuted for targeting them in a cyberstalking campaign that involved sending the couple cockroaches, fly larvae and a bloody Halloween pig mask.

As part of ⁠the settlement, eBay agreed to pay $46.15m to the couple; fund $6m in charitable contributions to non-profit organizations; and issue a “strongly-worded” statement about the conduct ​of three of its top former executives.

“We believe this resolution ‌sends a clear message that corporations and ‌their executives cannot engage in this type of misconduct without facing significant consequences,” Christopher Murphy, the Steiners’ attorney, said in a statement.

Ebay said ‌in a statement that what happened to the Steiners was “wrong, reprehensible and should never have happened”.

“We continue to extend our deepest apologies to the Steiners,” the company said. “This agreement is consistent with our commitment to fairly compensate the Steiners and fulfills our efforts to make things right.”

Seven former eBay workers pleaded guilty and received sentences of as high as 57 months in prison for participating in the scheme, which also involved several of them traveling from California to Natick, Massachusetts, to surveil the Steiners and try to install a GPS tracking ‌device on their car.

Prosecutors have said that the aim was to silence them after senior executives deemed their newsletter, EcommerceBytes, critical of the company. The campaign began after the then CEO, Devin Wenig, in August 2019 texted Steve Wymer, then ​its chief communications officer, that it was time to “take her down”, referring to Ina Steiner, according to prosecutors and the Steiners. Ebay itself was criminally charged and agreed in 2024 to pay a $3m fine.

Wenig, a former Thomson Reuters executive who stepped down as eBay’s CEO in September 2019, was never charged. His lawyers have argued he had no knowledge or involvement in the harassment campaign and that his messages had been advocating for a ⁠public relations strategy to address Ina Steiner’s reporting.

As part of the settlement, the Steiners’ attorneys said Wenig will ​pay them $2m and make a $1m ​donation to a charity focused on protecting first amendment ​rights in the name of Ina Steiner.

“No one should ever have been subjected to what the Steiners endured in ​2019, and I’m saddened by ‌it, especially because it occurred ​during my time as CEO ​of eBay,” Wenig said in a statement on Tuesday. “This behavior is antithetical to everything I stand for and believe in.“

Wendy Jones, who previously served as senior vice-president of global operations, and Wymer will pay the couple $500,000 and $50,000, respectively, the plaintiffs say. Their lawyers did not respond to requests for comment.

The Steiners’ lawyers said additional settlements were reached with all other eBay employees named in their lawsuit.

description:

The FCC defines the banned robots as “advanced robotic devices”, which include humanoids and animal-like quadrupeds.
