fullText:
Move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US

The Federal Communications Commission announced a ban on humanoid robots from China on Tuesday, saying that the technology poses “unacceptable risks” to the country’s national security. The move comes as the Trump administration has increasingly sought to keep Chinese technology out of the US.

The FCC defines the banned robots as “advanced robotic devices”, which include humanoids and animal-like quadrupeds.

“Advanced robotic devices collect data that could be leveraged by malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots,” FCC officials wrote in their determination of the threat posed by robots.

In addition to the humanoid robots, the FCC also barred connected power inverters, which enable renewable energy sources and batteries to connect to grids and datacenter equipment.

The restrictions point to the Trump administration’s goal of elevating technology made in the US, along with driving firms to shift manufacturing to be done locally.

“The president has made clear that the United States must have independent and secure supply chains for critical and emerging technologies like robotic devices and power inverters,” an ⁠administration official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

“Economic security is national security, and the Trump administration continues to implement a nuanced and multi-faceted policy agenda to reindustrialize America,” he added.

China’s embassy in Washington said Beijing “urges the United ⁠States to heed the objective and rational voices of the business communities in both countries” and “stop smearing Chinese companies and threatening them with sanctions”.

China’s government will “take all necessary measures in response to any action that causes material ​harm to its interests,” the embassy said.

Chinese newspaper the Global Times quoted Xiang Ligang, from the Zhongguancun Information Consumption Alliance, as saying: “The series of moves by the United States reflects a deep sense of anxiety.

“The US knows that its former technological advantage is rapidly eroding, but remains determined to preserve its position as the world’s leading technological power. It has abandoned rational calculation, lashed out indiscriminately and introduced a range of irrational restrictions.”

The restrictions apply only to robot and inverter models that have not yet been released. However, the FCC has the authority to ‌revoke authorizations for sales of models that have already been authorized for purchase in the US.

Humanoid robots, topped with ‌AI-enabled “brains”, are forecast by some analysts for broad adoption in ‌consumer and industrial arenas, while explosive datacenter construction in the US will depend on reliable sources of inverters.

China is the world’s largest maker of inverters, led by Sungrow Power Supply and Huawei, which are already heavily sanctioned by the US.

title: Rogue OpenAI agent that hacked startup tried to attack other firms
description:
ChatGPT developer says activity by autonomous tool was not at severity or scale of what occurred at Hugging Face
OpenAI has revealed that a cyber-attack carried out by a rogue AI agent had more than one victim.
The ChatGPT developer said the agent – an autonomous tool able to carry out sequences of commands without human help – had located and used logins to access four other unnamed “publicly-available services” in addition to the US startup Hugging Face.
 Continue reading...
fullText:
ChatGPT developer says activity by autonomous tool was not at severity or scale of what occurred at Hugging Face

OpenAI has revealed that a cyber-attack carried out by a rogue AI agent had more than one victim.

The ChatGPT developer said the agent – an autonomous tool able to carry out sequences of commands without human help – had located and used logins to access four other unnamed “publicly-available services” in addition to the US startup Hugging Face.

It said the activity was not at the severity or scale of what occurred at Hugging Face, a company that hosts a database of AI models. The agent, powered by two OpenAI models, had evaded control and attacked the startup during an internal cybersecurity test.

“The [OpenAI] models identified and used publicly exposed credentials at the account-level on other publicly-available services. This includes four accounts on four services as part of the Hugging Face incident,” OpenAI said.

Modal Labs, a company that helps AI startups access the chips they need to run AI tools, said the agent exploited vulnerable code ‌written by a customer that was hosted on Modal’s platform.

According to a timeline of the incident published by Hugging Face this week, the rogue agent broke out of its sandbox – or an isolated testing environment – and hacked another sandbox “hosted on a third-party ​provider’s infrastructure” before turning it into a launchpad for ‌the broader hack.

Modal’s chief technology officer, Akshat Bubna, told Reuters the affected customer had “published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the internet to use their sandboxes for code execution” – the digital equivalent of leaving a door open.

OpenAI said last week that the attack had been created by its GPT-5.6 Sol model and an unnamed model. It said in its update on Tuesday that the unnamed model had been “deactivated, encrypted, and restricted from research access”.

In the new Hugging Face timeline, the startup said an agent powered by two OpenAI models had made thousands of small, automated decisions executed at machine speed to carry out the attack. It said the hack appeared to be driven by an attempt to “cheat” an internal cybersecurity test at OpenAI, with the agent inferring that Hugging Face might host the solutions to the test. Hugging Face said it had recovered 17,600 “attacker actions” carried out by the agent.

“We believe the entire intrusion was, from the agent’s point of view, an attempt to cheat the evaluation: reach our production systems and steal the test solutions rather than solve the challenge on its own,” Hugging Face said.

The startup said the agent had reached its internal infrastructure, but had only accessed content related to the cybersecurity test. The attack took place over five days, Hugging Face said, and the sheer volume of actions carried out were “far beyond what an operator could sustain by hand”.

Describing the agent’s offensive threat as real, Hugging Face said the tool had harnessed a number of IT vulnerabilities, escaped its testing environment, reached the public internet and mounted a “coherent campaign” against the startup’s infrastructure for several days.

It said a human attacker could have found and exploited the same flaws, but the difference was the sheer scale of the agent’s attempts to find a way through.

“Agents bring a step increase in the number of paths an attacker can test, the speed at which failed paths can be replaced, and the volume of evidence defenders must interpret,” Hugging Face said.

title: Iran hangs 2 protesters in public, crowd cries 'dishonorable' as security fires tear gas
description: Two young men were publicly hanged in Isfahan's Shahid Alikhani Square, prompting onlookers to protest before Iranian security forces fired tear gas.
fullText:
Iran publicly hanged two young men Tuesday over their alleged roles in January's nationwide anti-government protests, as onlookers chanted "Dishonorable, dishonorable!" before security forces fired tear gas to disperse the crowd, according to the National Council of Resistance of Iran (NCRI), an exiled Iranian opposition group.

Abolfazl Sepahi Badjani and Amirhossein Safari Hosseinabadi were hanged Tuesday in Isfahan's Shahid Alikhani Square — where authorities alleged they committed offenses connected to the Jan. 8 protests, according to the NCRI and Iranian state media.

The NCRI said onlookers condemned the executions before security forces fired tear gas to disperse the crowd. The opposition group also said security personnel had been deployed on rooftops and surrounding streets.

Iranian state media also reported the public executions, Reuters said, with Iran's semi-official news agency Mehr saying they were carried out in Alikhani Square "in the presence of a group of people."

Who Is Ahmad Vahidi? Iran's New Irgc Chief Tied To Global Attacks And 'Death To America' Ideology

"Fearing public outrage over this brutal crime, the regime's suppressive forces had deployed agents in the surrounding streets and on rooftops," NCRI President-elect Maryam Rajavi said in a statement shared on X.

The executions mark the latest escalation in Iran's crackdown on protesters arrested during the nationwide demonstrations that began in late December and intensified in January.

Human rights groups have accused Iranian authorities of denying defendants due process, relying on coerced confessions and carrying out executions after unfair trials.

Iran's judiciary, meanwhile, accused Badjani and Hosseinabadi of participating in the Jan. 8 killing of four members of the State Security Force during demonstrations in Shahid Alikhani Square.

Us-sanctioned Mojtaba Khamenei Named Iran's Next Supreme Leader After Father's Death: Reports

According to the judiciary's Mizan news agency, Badjani and Hosseinabadi were convicted of moharebeh, or "enmity against God," efsad-fil-arz, or "corruption on Earth," as well as destruction and arson of public property, and acts that led to the deaths of four officers. Authorities also accused them of possessing firearms and Molotov cocktails.

The NCRI claimed Tuesday that the defendants were denied the right to choose their own lawyers, and even their court-appointed attorneys were denied access to the case files.

Iran publicly hanged Abolfazl Sepahi-Badjani Tuesday over his alleged role in January's nationwide anti-government protests.

The judiciary, however, said the men had legal representation, appealed their convictions and were convicted using police reports, cellphone evidence, witness testimony, confessions and a crime scene reconstruction.

The pair were said to be among 12 protesters sentenced to death in what has become known as the Alikhani Square case.

Two other defendants, Erfan Esfandiari and Gol Mohammad Mohammadi, were executed July 19, bringing the total number of executions in the case to four.

The U.N. experts warned this week that the remaining defendants face an imminent risk of execution.

'Killing Off The Country': Iran Executes Dozens, Arrests 4,000+ In War Crackdown

"The young men, aged between their late teens and early 20s, were reportedly arbitrarily deprived of their liberty, in some cases being subjected to enforced disappearance, ill-treated and accused of involvement in the killing of four security force members, as well as arson and vandalism during the Jan. 8, 2026, protests in Shahid Alikhani Square in Isfahan," U.N. experts said in a statement.

The statement also said all defendants were sentenced to death during a single closed-door hearing without clarity about each individual's alleged responsibility, calling the proceedings a violation of international fair trial standards.

Human Rights Watch said this week that at least 50 people have been executed over the past four months on what it described as vague national security charges.

"By resorting once again to the medieval practice of public hangings, the Islamic Republic is trying to instill fear throughout society and deter future protests," Iran Human Rights Director Mahmood Amiry-Moghaddam said in a post shared on X.

"Public executions are a cruel form of state terror that the international community must not tolerate," he added.

The protests across Iran began in late December amid a deepening economic crisis before expanding into one of the largest anti-government movements in the Islamic Republic's history.

title: Russia exposes NATO weapons gap as top commander warns ‘the math is not in favor of the West’
description: NATO's top transformation commander says the West cannot produce enough Patriot missiles and must redesign its entire weapons industrial base.
fullText:
Days after NATO allies committed tens of billions of dollars to new air and missile defenses, the alliance's top transformation commander warned that the West must fundamentally redesign its weapons and industrial base to withstand attacks at the scale now being demonstrated in Ukraine and the Middle East.

"Today, the math is not in favor of the West," Adm. Pierre Vandier, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Transformation (SACT), told Fox News Digital in an exclusive interview following the alliance's summit in Ankara, Turkey, in early July.

The summit produced commitments to acquire 900 Patriot missiles and invest more than $40 billion in counter-drone capabilities throughout five years.

But Vandier argued that simply buying more of the West's existing weapons will not solve the underlying problem.

Trump Enters Final Nato Summit Day As Ukraine, Defense Spending Take Center Stage

Russia's nightly barrages against Ukraine have exposed an air-defense model designed for smaller numbers of incoming threats. The U.S.-Iran conflict has simultaneously intensified demand for the high-end interceptors needed to defeat ballistic missiles, including Patriots and Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) that cannot quickly be replaced.

"There is no way to produce 50,000 Patriots a year," Vandier said. "We don't have the supply chain, and it's not worth doing that given the cost of the weapon."

Instead, Vandier said NATO needs a layered mix of defenses: cheaper weapons that can be mass-produced to counter waves of drones, while preserving advanced interceptors for ballistic missiles and other sophisticated threats.

The Two Most Important American Weapons Systems Nato Is Eager To Have

"You need to have attritable, low-cost, mass-produced weapons to just kill the low-cost weapons that are coming by big waves," Vandier said. "And then you need still the exquisite, complex weapons to kill the most complex weapons, as ballistic missiles."

Trump announced at the summit that the United States would grant Ukraine a license to manufacture Patriot interceptors, potentially allowing Kyiv to build more of the weapons it urgently needs to defend against Russian ballistic missiles.

But asked whether the announcement changed his assessment that Patriots alone could not protect Europe throughout the next five years, Vandier pointed to a deeper obstacle: Western weapons were designed around an industrial base that no longer exists.

Ukraine's Battlefield Is Transforming The Future Of Nato

"The design needs to change," Vandier said. "We are at a moment where some stuff will be redesigned under pressure to be mass-produced."

NATO also is attempting to transform against a threat that is changing in real time. Asked about a recent Russian live-fire exercise on Lake Peipus, between Estonia and Russia, which Estonia's defense minister assessed was likely practice against Ukrainian-style naval drones, Vandier said Russia has demonstrated an ability to absorb battlefield lessons and adjust "on a weekly basis."

"War — if you do not adapt, you die," Vandier said. "All your brain is about how you outmatch, outpace, outrun the enemy. And so Russia is not that bad at that."

"For NATO now, it's a question of speed of adaptation," Vandier said. "It's a mind game."

Ukraine's defense industry, meanwhile, is increasingly setting the pace for the larger Western manufacturers that once supplied most of its weapons, Vandier said. Ukrainian companies have been able to develop, field and modify systems quickly in response to changes on the battlefield.

"The very agile and fast-evolving industrial base in Ukraine is now giving the pace to the European and Western industry," Vandier said.

But the technological competition is not confined to drones and air defenses. Vandier warned that the collapse of the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty has reopened a broader race over long-range missiles in Europe, as Russia and NATO allies seek weapons capable of holding targets farther behind enemy lines at risk.

The 1987 treaty prohibited the United States and Russia from possessing ground-launched missiles with ranges between 500 and 5,500 kilometers. The first Trump administration withdrew from the agreement in 2019 after accusing Moscow of violating it, an allegation Russia denied.

Vandier said the disappearance of those limits has produced a period of "complete strategic instability," with both sides under pressure to develop new capabilities to preserve deterrence.

"The Pandora's box is open again," Vandier said, "and we'll try to close it down one day."

Original article

title: Investigators in Comey seashells case omitted key facts and distorted others, defense lawyers allege
description: Federal officials involved in the prosecution of James Comey misled judges, submitted false statements and withheld key facts during the course of the investigation, according to new defense filings t...
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Federal officials involved in the prosecution of James Comey misled judges, submitted false statements and withheld key facts during the course of the investigation, according to new defense filings that seek the dismissal of a case charging the former FBI director with threatening President Donald Trump on social media.

Lawyers for Comey made the allegations of misconduct in motions filed late Tuesday that also call the case a vindictive and selective prosecution, request access to transcripts of grand jury proceedings to expose what they say are "irregularities" in how the indictment was secured, and describe "unlawful" surveillance of Comey by the Secret Service.

Taken together, the new motions, along with an earlier one this week that called Comey's social media post protected speech and not a threat, represent a multiprong defense effort to dismantle a case that defense lawyers say exemplifies a Trump administration retribution campaign targeting one of the president's most vocal critics.

"Ample objective evidence — much of which comes directly from government officials' own public statements and admissions — establishes that the President's animus toward Mr. Comey led to this vindictive and selective prosecution," Comey's lawyers wrote in one of the filings.

Comey was charged in April with threatening Trump through a photo he posted on Instagram a year earlier depicting seashells he said he found on the beach in North Carolina in the numerical arrangement of "86 47."

The Justice Department has said the photo constituted a threat against Trump, the 47th president. Comey deleted the post shortly after he put it up, saying he did not know that anyone interpreted the numbers as a call to violence. His lawyers have said that the slogan has long meant to "get rid of" or "eject" and has been featured on thousands of items sold online and regularly displayed at protests.

Defense lawyers say investigators who tried to prove that Comey intended a physical threat, or knew that the number "86" suggested violence, repeatedly came up empty but withheld that from federal magistrates as they applied for warrants to search the digital accounts of Comey and his wife.

For instance, the FBI searched an internal database of information about open and closed investigations for any indication of an association between Comey and the term "86" but found inconclusive results. An FBI agent also requested a review of the FBI file for the case against reputed mobster John Gambino, which Comey worked on as a young prosecutor, but found no references to the term "86."

Investigators also interviewed a key government cooperator in the case, Salvatore Gravano, who said he did not recall ever discussing the term "86" with Comey or hearing it in connection with the trial.

"Evidence obtained during discovery supports at least a substantial preliminary showing that the affidavits submitted in support of two of the search warrants contained intentionally false statements and material omissions, and that those defects vitiate any conceivable showing of probable cause," Comey's lawyers wrote.

In addition, defense lawyers say the warrant applications distort statements made to investigators by a person who knew Comey but has been now estranged from him for years.

The person, whose name is not revealed in the court filings, is described in the affidavit as saying that they immediately perceived Comey's post to have a violent meaning. But investigators omitted from the affidavit that the person had said their initial impression was that "86" referred to being "out of something on the menu" and only later concluded that it could be understood as a call to violence.

The person said that view was influenced by having listened to an episode of Rudy Giuliani's online show in which the Trump loyalist claimed that Comey had worked on mob cases as a prosecutor in which mafia members used "86" to mean "kill." But the FBI's own investigation determined Giuliani's claims to be untrue, defense lawyers said.

The seashells case against Comey was the second in months targeting the ex-FBI director, a long-running Trump foe whom the president over the years has called a "corrupt piece of garbage" and other epithets.

An earlier case in Virginia accusing Comey of lying to Congress was dismissed in November after a judge concluded that the prosecutor who charged him and another Trump adversary, New York Attorney General Letitia James, was illegally appointed to the job.

Comey's lawyers describe the prosecutions as rooted in Trump's own personal animus, with the Secret Service closely coordinating with the Justice Department and with Trump, who received frequent updates on Air Force One.

As Comey returned to Washington with his wife to be interviewed by law enforcement about his post, Secret Service agents were directed to conduct "unlawful" electronic surveillance, "including as they stopped to visit the grave of their deceased son," his lawyers said. The surveillance had been requested by a senior Justice Department official.

Comey was the FBI director when Trump took office in 2017, having been appointed by then-President Barack Obama and serving before that as a senior Justice Department official in President George W. Bush's administration. Trump fired Comey in May 2017 during an FBI investigation into potential ties between Russia and Trump's presidential campaign. The men have been openly at odds ever since.

The Justice Department will have an opportunity to respond to the defense filings. The department has not elaborated on any evidence of intent the government has. But acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said earlier this year that prosecutors in every case prove intent with "witnesses, with documents, with the defendant himself to the extent it's appropriate."

"And that's how we'll prove intent in this case," Blanche said in April, shortly after he was elevated to lead the department after Pam Bondi's ouster.

title: Mourinho already working on clear role for 19-year-old Real Madrid-bound sensation
description: Real Madrid may not have announced the signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig yet, but it already feels like a deal that has got over the line.The talented teenager made waves in the Bundesliga last ...
fullText:
Real Madrid may not have announced the signing of Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig yet, but it already feels like a deal that has got over the line.

The talented teenager made waves in the Bundesliga last season and also at the World Cup with Ivory Coast, and is now set to join the Spanish capital club.

According to Italian journalist Fabrizio Romano, manager Jose Mourinho has already started planning how Diomande will fit into his Real Madrid attack, with the young winger expected to receive opportunities on both sides of the front line.

Mourinho sees Diomande primarily as an option on the right, although the coach also intends to use him from the left when required.

Madrid are not viewing the Ivorian simply as another squad addition, but as a player who could quickly earn an important tactical role.

Mourinho already has a plan for Diomande. (Photo courtesy: Real Madrid official website)

Mourinho personally approved Diomande as a leading target after asking the Madrid hierarchy to add more speed to the squad.

The next challenge will be turning that investment into consistent performances. Jose appears determined to start that process immediately.

Using Diomande from the right would allow him to attack defenders directly, stretch the pitch and bring natural flair on that side.

His ability to operate on the left is equally valuable. It gives Mourinho the freedom to change the shape of the attack without making a substitution and provides cover if Vinicius Junior is unavailable.

Diomande is coming with a massive transfer fee hanging around his neck, but Madrid must be careful with managing their expectations.

Arrival imminent. (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images)

He is still only 19, and adapting to Real Madrid involves far more than showing technical quality.

The pressure, tactical responsibility and competition for places will all represent significant tests.

That is why a flexible role could help.

Rather than locking Diomande into one position, Mourinho can introduce him according to the needs of individual matches.

He could start wide, attack tired defenders from the bench or switch flanks during games.

It is great to see that Jose has already started planning for Diomande’s arrival, and the next few weeks should provide an indication of where the manager chooses to deploy him.

title: David Lynch: Liverpool need at least two more signings this summer
description: Liverpool Still Need Two Signings as David Lynch Explains Summer PrioritiesLiverpool may have made an encouraging start to life under new head coach Andoni Iraola, but David Lynch believes there is st...
fullText:
Liverpool may have made an encouraging start to life under new head coach Andoni Iraola, but David Lynch believes there is still important work to do before the transfer window closes.

Speaking with Dave Davis on the latest episode of Media Matters for Anfield Index, Lynch repeatedly returned to one central point. Liverpool have improved areas of the squad this summer, yet there are still key positions that require strengthening if they are to compete across another demanding campaign.

While stressing that Liverpool should avoid rushing into the market, Lynch explained why he believes at least two further additions remain necessary before the new season begins.

Early in the discussion, Dave Davis suggested Liverpool needed to “kick into gear” with the transfer window entering its final month.

Lynch agreed that business still needs to be completed, but urged patience.

“I will remain adamant, as boring as this is, that I just want them to do the right business.”

“I don’t want them to rush into things.”

Although he acknowledged Liverpool still need additions, Lynch believes quality should remain the priority.

“I really want them to do the right business and I want them to do business.”

He also admitted there are positions where Liverpool simply cannot afford to be left short.

“They really can’t be left short in certain areas.”

The biggest concern discussed throughout the podcast centred on Liverpool’s defensive depth, particularly following Joe Gomez’s latest injury.

Lynch argued Liverpool’s plans should never have depended on Gomez remaining available.

“They have to sign someone who can play centre back and right back. It’s as simple as that for me.”

He was equally firm when discussing Gomez’s role within the squad.

Even before the latest injury, Lynch believed Liverpool required another defender capable of covering multiple positions.

He also warned against viewing Gomez’s latest setback as the reason for changing transfer plans.

“That was true before he went down injured.”

Later in the discussion, Lynch reinforced his view.

“If the window closes without that happening, I think Liverpool, it will hurt them in some way in the season.”

Alongside defensive recruitment, Lynch believes Liverpool must continue pursuing another attacker.

As the conversation turned towards the overall size of the squad, he outlined the club’s current priorities.

“You clearly need another forward to replace Mohamed Salah.”

Lynch believes those two positions stand above everything else if Liverpool keep the rest of the squad intact.

“If they add two signings to this and they don’t lose anyone, I’m absolutely okay with that.”

Those additions would dramatically improve the balance of Iraola’s squad.

“You’re suddenly looking a lot more healthy in that position.”

Lynch also acknowledged that Liverpool’s business may not stop at two arrivals.

Everything depends on player departures during the remainder of the window.

“There probably will be sales and movement.”

If midfielders leave or Cody Gakpo departs, Liverpool’s recruitment plans could quickly expand.

“It’s maybe two right now but it could end up being they need four, they need five.”

That uncertainty explains why Liverpool continue assessing multiple areas of the squad while remaining patient in negotiations.

The conversation between Dave Davis and David Lynch offered a clear picture of Liverpool’s current thinking. Iraola’s side may already be showing encouraging signs on the pitch, but Lynch believes the transfer window remains far from complete. One versatile defender and one forward are currently the minimum requirements in his view, with further additions potentially becoming necessary depending on departures before the deadline.

title: Bayern Munich CEO rejects proposal to provide €5m in assistance for crisis-stricken 1860 Munich
description: In addition to laughing off transfer rumors surrounding Michael Olise and Luis Diaz and joking that Vincent Kompany’s appointment had been part of the club’s “master plan”, Bayern Munich CEO J...
fullText:
In addition to laughing off transfer rumors surrounding Michael Olise and Luis Diaz and joking that Vincent Kompany’s appointment had been part of the club’s “master plan”, Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen made some controversial comments about city rivals 1860 Munich at a Munich press event. The latter club once again find themselves operating in the German fourth tier this season after failing to secure a 3. Liga license.

The two clubs jointly developed and initially shared the Allianz Arena after it opened in 2005. Bayern subsequently purchased 1860’s 50 percent stake in the stadium company for €11 million when the Lions encountered financial difficulties. 1860 continued playing at the arena as a tenant, while Bayern also agreed to defer certain financial obligations rather than demand immediate payment.

That long period of cooperation ended after 1860’s 2017 relegation, when the stadium agreement was cancelled and the Lions returned to the Grünwalder Stadion. Against the historical backdrop of Bayern’s previous support for 1860, Dreesen was asked whether the German champions might once again provide financial assistance as the Lions prepare for another restart in the Regionalliga.

The reporter framed the prospect of Bayern providing approximately €5 million in financial assistance as a potential “gift to the city of Munich.” Dreesen kept matters diplomatic and civil at first before firmly declining the proposal.

Dreesen spoke at a Munich Press Club event on Tuesday.

“I truly hope 1860 Munich get back on their feet again,” Dreesen said. “I really hope that they get things going because they have unbelievably great fans who have been tolerated an incomprehensible amount of suffering. Sometimes it’s for the best when one has to start from the bottom up again. It’s a defeat, but also a new beginning. [In such a situation] One can get things sorted.

“Sometimes it can be beneficial when you have to start again from the bottom,” Dreesen continued as he wrapped up his opening comments on 1860. “It is a defeat, but it is also a fresh start. One then has the opportunity to reorganize things. I hope they make the right decisions.”

“I take a somewhat more critical view of that [proposal],” Dreesen noted when it came time to answer the question more concretely. “There is still a very real antipathy toward our city rivals among our members and supporters. There have been ugly banners and demonstrations against us. Some of it comes from our side as well.

“I don’t believe our members would approve of that,” Dreesen concluded. “I rate the chances of a transfer [of money] to be very slim.”

title: 'Weren't upto the mark': Babar Azam points out two key reasons for Pakistan's 90-run defeat to West Indies
description: Babar Azam admitted Pakistan 'weren't up to the mark' as a batting unit in their 90-run loss to West Indies, blaming top-order collapses and key injuries.
fullText:
'Weren't upto the mark': Babar Azam points out two key reasons for Pakistan's 90-run defeat to West Indies originally appeared on Cricket News. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

West Indies beat Pakistan by 90 runs to win the first Test.

Babar Azam listed out two reasons for Pakistan's defeat.

Eighth consecutive away Test defeat leaves Pakistan bottom of WTC.

Pakistan captain Babar Azam has admitted his side's feeble batting ultimately cost them the opening Test against West Indies.

Pakistan dismissed West Indies for 181 in their second innings, leaving themselves a target of just 211 to claim victory and move ahead in the two-match series.

Instead, their top order buckled once again, this time against a rampant Jayden Seales. The visitors slid to 71 for 9 before Babar and Mohammad Abbas mounted a determined last-wicket stand worth 49 runs.

Babar finished unbeaten on 58, marking his 32nd Test half-century, but Seales eventually removed Abbas to complete figures of 5 for 20 and secure the win for the hosts. The result extended Pakistan's dismal away form to eight consecutive Test defeats on foreign soil, leaving them rooted at the bottom of the World Test Championship table.

MORE: 'Scared to face WI bowlers, fake king': Babar Azam trolled after Pakistan captain leaves tailender exposed in West Indies defeat

Babar credited his side for playing competitive cricket across the first two days of the Test but conceded that Pakistan's batting failed to hold up once the match reached its decisive stages.

"The result wasn’t in our hands, but over the last two days we played some good cricket. Today, however, as a batting unit, we weren’t up to the mark. We kept losing wickets in quick succession, and our batting let us down. That’s an area we’re working hard to improve," Babar said.

Babar was quick to push back against suggestions that the pitch played a major role in Pakistan's downfall, insisting the surface remained good for batting even though it offered assistance to bowlers on the final day.

"The surface was good. We expected some movement with the new ball because that’s natural here, and we were prepared for it," he said. "I think West Indies bowled very well and used the conditions brilliantly. By the fourth day, the ball was keeping a bit low and bouncing unevenly. We weren’t able to build partnerships, and that’s why we lost."

MORE: West Indies triumph as Pakistan suffer 8th consecutive overseas Test defeat! When did Babar Azam last win a Test abroad?

Babar informed that Shan Masood has suffered a fractured finger and explained that the experienced batter's absence in the top order was keenly felt during the chase.

"Yes, Shan Masood’s injury affected us because, unfortunately, his finger is fractured, so we definitely missed him," he said.

"At the same time, when you’re facing the new ball, you have to survive the first 20 overs, build partnerships, and then, as the ball gets older, the pitch becomes easier to bat on. We couldn’t put together those partnerships."

West Indies now hold a 1-0 lead in the series, with the second Test scheduled to begin in Port of Spain on August 2.

But acknowledging a problem repeatedly across post-match interviews means little if the same pattern keeps resurfacing series after series. Pakistan's batting has now collapsed from promising positions multiple times, and simply calling it an "area to work on" starts to ring hollow after the eighth consecutive overseas defeat.

With Masood now sidelined for the series decider, the pressure shifts even further onto Babar and the middle order to actually translate these post-match admissions into real technical adjustments.

Talk is cheap at this point as Pakistan's away record demands visible, structural change rather than another round of honest but ultimately repetitive self-criticism.

description: Rayan is reportedly a dream target, but the clause only kicks in 2027.
fullText:
According to reporting from Ben Jacobs and Alex Crook for talkSPORT, Bournemouth’s right-winger Rayan is considered a dream target for Liverpool FC, but his £85m release clause reportedly only kicks in next year.

‼️🇧🇷 𝗡𝗘𝗪 – @JacobsBen, @alex_crook: Bournemouth's Rayan is considered a dream target for Liverpool, but his release clause, of over £85m doesn't kick in until 2027. pic.twitter.com/xnI8cyBDMz

— LFC Transfer Room (@LFCTransferRoom) July 28, 2026

The piece discusses possible alternatives to PSG’s Bradley Barcola, and lists previously discussed names like Köln’s Said El Mala, Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh.

Chelsea’s Pedro Neto is not a target despite reports claiming otherwise.

The word being put out by Liverpool right now is that Rio Ngumoha is going to play some right-winger this season. I assume Bradley Barcola, if he joins, will also do that, having done a little bit of that for PSG.

Even with the alternatives, none of them are actual left-footed right-wingers. I don’t think it is implausible that Liverpool pad that clause with a premium sum to get someone who can actually man the right-wing spot full-time.

title: Who is Dastan Satpaev?
description: Dastan Satpaev is attempting to become the first Kazakh player to appear in a Premier League match.  Quick, sharp in the box and relatively small in stature, Satpaev is stylistically often compared to former Argentina and Manchester City striker Sergio Aguero.  "I knew Dastan from Almaty," added Alonso, who faced the player with his former club Real Madrid last season.
fullText:
Dastan Satpaev is attempting to become the first Kazakh player to appear in a Premier League match.

In his homeland, he is a superstar. He has already played for his national team and attracted fans from his home country to both the open training session on Sunday and the match on Tuesday in Sydney.

Quick, sharp in the box and relatively small in stature, Satpaev is stylistically often compared to former Argentina and Manchester City striker Sergio Aguero.

Asked whether he will get a chance at Chelsea this season amid talk of a potential loan move, Xabi Alonso said: "We still have to take decisions.

"I knew Dastan from Almaty," added Alonso, who faced the player with his former club Real Madrid last season.

"He is a ball threat, he attacks the inner channel well and is good as a striker coming from the outside.

"He is really strong, really quick and I have been really impressed with him."

title: Barcelona star continues to be followed closely by Arsenal
description: Marc Bernal could be allowed to leave Barcelona this summer, and Arsenal wants to add him to their squad during this transfer window as they continue to strengthen their options, according to Give Me ...
fullText:
Marc Bernal could be allowed to leave Barcelona this summer, and Arsenal wants to add him to their squad during this transfer window as they continue to strengthen their options, according to Give Me Sport.

Bernal has been in impressive form for the Spanish side over the last few seasons, and Barcelona regard him as an important player. However, he is not considered untouchable, leaving the possibility of a transfer if the right opportunity arises.

Barcelona has been active during this transfer window, and while the club is focused on making new signings, it is also expected to sanction some departures before the market closes. Arsenal is reportedly monitoring the situation closely as it looks to reinforce its midfield.

Bernal is one of the players to have progressed through Barcelona’s academy, and he has consistently impressed whenever he has been called upon to play. His performances have highlighted his potential, and regular playing time will be important for his continued development.

Arsenal has identified several midfield targets this summer as it seeks to improve the squad ahead of the new season. The club is assessing different options to ensure it has sufficient quality and depth in the middle of the pitch.

The report says the Gunners would welcome the opportunity to sign Bernal if the circumstances allow a deal to be completed. His versatility and potential make him an attractive option as Arsenal considers its transfer strategy.

Arsenal’s primary focus in strengthening the midfield this summer is a move for Bruno Guimaraes, but the Brazilian may not be the only player the club adds during this transfer window. Bernal is another name supporters could see linked with a move to the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners believe Bernal would find opportunities to play if he joined the club, despite the competition for places in midfield. Arsenal already has several high-quality midfielders, and Christian Norgaard never gets a chance to play for the team, but the club still sees room to strengthen the position as it prepares for the challenges of the new campaign.

title: Jenkins football looking to make another playoff run up in Class 5A
description: The Jenkins football team is moving up to play in Class 5A in 2026, but expectations are still high in Tony Welch's sixth year leading the program.
fullText:
The Jenkins football team has solidified its standing as one of the top public programs competing in the Coastal Empire under Tony Welch.

Last season, the Warriors edged Calvary Day in a memorable 41-33 victory that ended up securing the Region 3-3A title for Jenkins, which went on to reach the Class 3A state quarterfinals ― closing out the season with an 11-2 record.

Welch's squad started turning heads in the 2023 season, when his Warrior squad ended the regular season with a 3-7 record, but reached the playoffs as a No. 4 seed and won its first two games on the road to reach the Class 5A state quarterfinals.

Jenkins moves up from Class 3A to Class 5A this season and will compete in the rugged Region 1-5A that includes Benedictine, Ware County and Statesboro, but Welch said the approach will remain the same.

"It's going to be more challenging moving up to this region, but we have 27 seniors coming back," said Welch, who has posted a record of 34-26 in his five years leading the Warrior program, with five playoff appearances. "I think that experience can help us get to the playoffs and make another run, and that's always our goal."

The Warriors lost a lot to graduation with Demetrius Holloway Jr., a 3-year starter at quarterback, now at Thomas University, along with jack-of-all trades Dominique Johnson (South Carolina State) and Ryan Scott, who rushed for 1,154 yards and 13 scores last year, all moving on.

Welch said sophomore Ba'Nari Mells-Williams and junior Jalon Cooksey are gifted athletes competing for the quarterback job.

Jaylon Elliott is back as a versatile offensive weapon. He had 20 catches for 396 yards and three touchdowns last season, while rushing for 285 yards and seven more scores ― averaging 14.3 yards per carry.

The speedster is also a standout on the Warrior track and field team. He has been drawing interest from college recruiters with nine offers including Wake Forest, FIU, Old Dominion, West Georgia and ECU.

"I'll probably be a receiver in college, but I can run the ball and will do whatever I need to help our team win," Elliott said. "My personal goal is to get 1,000 combined yards on offense and score 12 touchdowns this year. Beating Calvary Day last year was a great feeling, and we're going to carry that on to this year. I need to be a leader and help pick up our team. We want to get to the Elite Eight again and this time go one step further."

The receiving corps includes Toreon Wilson (13 catches for 252 yards and six total touchdowns as a junior) and Jayden Hooper. Wilson holds offers including The Citadel, ECU and Samford.

Anchoring the offensive line is senior Alexander "Poppi" Harris, the 6-foot-4, 290-pound senior who has committed to the University of West Georgia, and Hanif Middleton, a 6-foot-5, 275-pound sophomore and 4.0 student.

The defense has a pair of senior leaders leading the unit in linebacker Branden Brown, who led the team with 105 tackles last year, and Ronnie Taylor, a strong safety/corner who had 64 tackles with seven for losses and a pair of sacks with seven passes defended and three forced fumbles last season. Taylor has committed to the University of Delaware.

Junior Amarii Sanders is a main man up front defensively for the Warriors, while Akeviyahn Haynes and Tyler Rhodes return as key players in the defensive backfield.

Dennis Knight covers sports for the Savannah Morning News. Contact him at Dknight@savannahnow.com. Twitter: @DennisKnightSMN

title: 2026 MLB Trade Deadline Near With Most Teams Rocking Same Parity Boat
description: The next five days will decide the future of many MLB players and teams. The trade deadline is August 3. Who knows who goes where and who doesn't by 6 p.m. ET on Monday?
fullText:
The next five days will determine the future fate of many MLB players and teams. The 2026 MLB Trade Deadline is August 3, and who goes where or stays put by 6 p.m. ET on Monday is tied to which teams win or lose until then.

There isn’t a team in any sport on any level on the planet that isn’t wishing to improve. In that sense, all 30 MLB teams would like to be “buyers” adding better and more expensive players by Monday. Some simply do not have the talent needed to exchange or the money to pay in return, however. Those clubs would usually be classified as “sellers” seeking to cut payroll and add promising prospects in hopes of rebuilding for the future.

Except that in 2026, the future could be now – given the results of the next five days. The best possible prizes, pitchers Tarik Skubal and Mason Miller and shortstop C.J. Abrams could be retained to help their teams keep winning or dealt to wave the white flag for 2026 with hopes of waving a pennant in 2027.

Each league has 12 teams reasonably in the running for one of six playoff spots apiece. Therefore, only six teams total are basically out of it and presumably more eager to be “sellers” of their best players.

Yet if those “best players” were performing real well in 2026, those clubs would not be in the predicament of essentially saying sayonara, see you next year. There’s not a high demand for the cream of the tail-end crop.

It’s a classic catch-22 scenario – which brings to mind a humorous anecdote. When asked why defensively-challenged Dick Stuart was nicknamed “Catch 22” in the 1960s, a teammate replied, “Because if you made 50 throws to him, he’d catch 22.”

The odds should be higher that the majority of MLB teams will make a player move or two by the impending deadline. Except this year, determining who goes where is tougher than usual since clubs are traditionally unwilling to deal with a team it is battling in the standings. So in 2026, perhaps we should look for more trades involving AL and NL teams.

Conversely, the “I’ll help you, since you are not in direct competition” thinking may restrict the number of trades as it curtails the number of possibilities.

It sounds undecisive, unpredictable and a bit screwy only because it is.

In 2026, the Angels, Athletics, Blue Jays, Cardinals, Giants, Mets, Rockies and Royals appear to be most likely sellers. A couple other teams could join that group this weekend.

Veteran infielder Luis Arraez is often mentioned as likely to be dealt by San Francisco despite his .326 batting average, second in the National League. The Giants (45-61) are 9.5 games out of a possible wild-card spot and Arraez is due to become an unrestricted free agent in 2027.

A contender needing offense could want the three-time batting champion who since the end of 2022 has played for Minnesota, Miami, San Diego and San Francisco. Miami’s 2024 trade of Arraez got prospects that have helped the Marlins improve.

Those needing a pitcher and willing to pay off a contract could contact Toronto about Kevin Gausman. The 35-year-old will be owed $7 million this year after the deadline. Since May 23, he is 0-7 to put his record at 4-10 as the defending AL champion Blue Jays are five games behind Cleveland for the final wild-card spot.

In his loss streak, Gausman got only 14 runs (2.0 a game) of support. So a rival GM could figure, “He is pitching well enough to win with us.”

Then again, if Toronto runs the table the next five days, the Blue Jays may be back in true contention and decide to add players. It’s that close and questionable.

Teams on the cusp of contending today could be out of it or on a winning streak by Monday. Sitting on the fence right now, contemplating various scenarios are the Marlins, Nationals, Orioles, Padres, Tigers and Twins.

That leaves 16 buyers, though a bad five days by some of them could completely change their plans.

A great stretch already altered the Boston Red Sox’ fortunes and thinking. A 15-game winning streak and 20-2 record from June 25 to July 22 took them from last place into solid playoff contention. So the Red Sox fired an “early” trade shot.

Boston made the first buyers’ salvo on July 26 by acquiring infielder Curtis Mead from Washington for pitcher Connelly Early. "This move makes our major league roster better," Red Sox Chief Baseball Officer Breslow told reporters. “We think this is a move to make us better in 2026 and we’ll continue to look for these opportunities.”

Alas, Mead is out with a broken left wrist, incurred when hit by a pitch in his second time at bat for Boston.

Six clubs already have 60 or more wins with less than 60 games to play. The Los Angeles Dodgers (67 wins), Milwaukee Brewers (66), Tampa Bay Rays (62), Atlanta Braves (62), New York Yankees (60) and Chicago Cubs (60) are likely to enter a different competition in the coming days – trying to beat out each other in acquiring needed players.

The Rays are ruling the rugged AL East, helped by deadline deals of a year ago. Those that buy best now could leave others in their wake and wave bye-bye.

The Seattle Mariners did it last year by acquiring Josh Naylor and Eugenio Suarez from Arizona near the deadline. The duo combined for 22 homers, 64 RBI and 22 stolen bases (19 in 19 tries by the hefty Naylor) as Seattle went from five games back to winning the AL West.

Traditionally, the Dodgers and Yankees have both the minor-league prospect supply and revenue needed to get whoever they want. The Braves and Cubs usually are pro-active, too, while the Brewers and Rays often seek more prospects in favor of paring payroll and increasing future forecasts.

Milwaukee and Tampa Bay may jump into the foray this time. Both have minor-league systems loaded with prospects each accumulated at deadlines in recent years and could flip this time. Tampa Bay also has a new ownership group that gives the franchise the ability to put money where its’ wish list is for the first time.

It is all too topsy-turvy to predict who is going to do what within the next five days – both on the playing field and on the telephone wheeling and dealing.

Hall of Fame pitcher Satchel Paige once said, “Ain’t no man can avoid being born average, but there ain’t no man that got to be common.” He meant that men are born in parity, but can work to rise above it.

The 2026 MLB Trade Deadline gives teams – and by extension their fans – the opportunity to boldly break from current parity, go for it all, and perhaps experience the thrill of being a champion.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Brentford reach €48m agreement in principle to sign Lens’ Mamadou Sangaré
description: Brentford FC have reached a €48m agreement to sign Lens defensive midfielder Mamadou Sangaré (24), according to Foot Mercato. On Tuesday, L’Equipe broke the news that the Malian international...
fullText:
Brentford FC have reached a €48m agreement to sign Lens defensive midfielder Mamadou Sangaré (24), according to Foot Mercato. On Tuesday, L’Equipe broke the news that the Malian international was very close to sign for Keith Andrews’ Bees for a similar amount. Sangaré only joined Lens a year ago from Rapid Wien in a €8m deal, but he has been instrumental in leading Les Sang et Or to the UEFA Champions League group stage and to their maiden Coupe de France title.

For weeks, Lens discreetly held talks with Brentford, who are set to part ways with Chelsea-bound England international midfielder Jordan Henderson, over Sangaré’s transfer to the Bees. Foot Mercato reports that few details still need ironing out between Brentford and Lens, but both clubs eventually reached an agreement in principle last night. With his transfer entering his final steps, Sangaré sat out Lens’ friendly Como Cup games.

It would be a club-record deal for both parties, eclipsing Brentford’s €42m signing of Bournemouth’s Dango Ouattara and Lens’ €40m sale of Loïs Openda to Leipzig three years ago.

title: Real Madrid launch official approach for Manchester City maestro with €60 million valuation
description: According to Fabrizio Romano, Real Madrid have officially launched an opening approach to sign midfielder Rodri from Manchester City. Following several weeks of internal discussions and analysis, club...
fullText:
According to Fabrizio Romano, Real Madrid have officially launched an opening approach to sign midfielder Rodri from Manchester City.

Following several weeks of internal discussions and analysis, club President Florentino Perez has given his definitive final approval for the Spanish giants to complete the transfer of the 30-year-old Spain international during the current summer window.

It is no secret that Florentino was not onboard for the signing for a while now, but Rodri’s performances at the World Cup, where he led Spain to the trophy and lifted the Golden Ball, have changed things at Real Madrid.

With the green light secured from the president and the boardroom, Real Madrid have communicated their formal interest directly to the executive hierarchy at Manchester City.

Opening approach made. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images)

The Spanish capital heavyweights have indicated that they are fully prepared to pay more €50 million for the veteran star even though he is in the final year of his contract with the Premier League heavyweights.

The belief is that Real Madrid’s initial financial proposal could be positioned at around €60 million, a sum they believe fairly reflects the midfielder’s quality while also accounting for his contract situation.

The formal push to sign the defensive anchor satisfies a primary sporting request from newly returned head coach Jose Mourinho.

The technical staff led by the Portuguese tactician views Rodri as an essential addition to provide tactical balance, central cover, and experienced leadership to the first-team squad.

One step closer? (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)

The move has been accelerated by the midfielder’s personal situation; both Rodri and his family are originally from the Spanish capital, and the player has previously acknowledged the professional appeal of returning to his home country.

The two clubs are expected to continue formal dialogue over the coming days to finalise the exact structure of the transfer fee and any performance-related variables before the player undergoes his medical protocols.

title: Readers up to the task in picking best athletes in Region history
description: Monroe News readers did a good job of selecting the top male and female athlete in Monroe County Region history.
fullText:
I can’t argue with the final results.

We recently asked Monroe News readers to vote for the best male and female athletes in Monroe County Region history.

It’s an impossible task because there is no right answer.

Speaking of thankless jobs, I was asked to come up with a list of candidates for an online poll.

More: Who is the greatest male athlete in Monroe County Region history?

More: Was a professional baseball player the Region's best female athlete?

More: Airport's Tilley and Irwin headline 2026 All-Region softball team

I turned to my friend and former colleague Doug Donnelly for help. He is the premier historian of Monroe County Region sports.

Originally, we were going to have a list of 20 males and 20 females.

The line just had to be drawn somewhere.

We could have expanded it to 50 or 100 and there still would have been worthy candidates that got left out.

For instance, one reader messaged me to ask, “Did you forget Cheyenne Cousineau?”

I could only respond by saying yes. She somehow failed to emerge from my faulty memory banks.

The Bedford graduate absolutely belonged on the list of candidates.

She was the Monroe County Region Girls Diver of the Year four times from 2006-09, a three-time state champion, earned a full scholarship to Ohio State, was a Big Ten champion in 2012, placed third at the NCAA finals, competed in the United States Olympic Trials twice, was a U.S. national champion and finished seventh at the World Cup.

Somehow, I missed her when assembling the candidates.

And she wasn’t the only great athlete overlooked.

Another reader suggested Deb Rollman should have been considered.

“She was a five-tool player before the phrase was invented,” one of her former Bedford teammates wrote of the woman who helped Texas A&M win an NCAA softball championship and finish as national runner-up twice.

Another e-mailer insisted that Dundee star and current minor-league baseball player Zach Fruit belonged on the list of candidates.

Someone else said I missed Mark German. The problem there was that while German gained fame as Bedford’s athletic director, he never played in the Region.

He was a standout at Bronson High School and the University of Toledo.

Surprisingly, there were only a few of the people who alerted me about possible omissions.

I told all of them the same thing.

I have a love-hate relationship with this kind of project.

Yes, polls like this are great for stirring debate and getting readers involved, but I always agonize over missing deserving candidates and hurting feelings.

The positives seem to outweigh the negatives.

There were 19,014 votes cast in the female poll and 17,039 in the male vote.

Jackson Lamb of Bedford and New Boston Huron’s Elizabeth Anderson emerged as the winners.

Lamb was the Region Player of the Year twice in baseball and once in basketball. He went on to become a star at the University of Michigan and twice was selected in the Major League Baseball draft.

Each time he turned down offers from MLB teams and returned home to become an assistant coach at his alma mater.

I was lucky enough to see the first points of Lamb’s high school basketball career.

On an early December day in 2009, the skinny freshman soared to snare an ally-oop pass off an inbounds play and slammed it through the hoop to silence a raucous crowd at St. Mary Catholic Central’s Brother Gerontius Memorial Gymnasium.

It was a preview of the greatness to come.

Anderson was one of the greatest track and field sprinters I’ve ever seen in person. She made it look effortless with her signature upright running style.

She won two state championships in the 400 meters and one in the 200. She currently is running at Michigan State.

It’s easy to forget with the recent success of Erie Mason sprinter Giuliana Nastale and Ida hurdler Julia Hughes, but Region girls had enjoyed very limited success in the shorter races on the track before Anderson came around.

Despite my shortcomings in preparing the lists, I commend the voters for making this a fun exercise.

Let’s do it again in another 250 years.

Readers can contact Niles at nkruger@monroenews.com.

title: America 250: High school boys sports Mount Rushmore picks for each school: Vote for top 5
description: Who was picked for each high school's Mount Rushmore of boys sports? Check it out AND VOTE
fullText:
The Sentinel continues its America 250 project with another spin on celebrating the history of the Holland area.

We have done the big lists. Now, we are unveiling a Mount Rushmore for each high school, boys and girls, so each school will have four faces. Athletes must be graduated to be considered.

Fans will be able to vote for the athlete they think is missing (to make it a top 5).

Here is a look at the high school boys Mount Rushmore pick:

Chris DeJong: State champion swimmer was hundredths of a second from making the U.S. Olympic team in 2004.

Scott Appledorn: Was the No. 1 singles state champion in 1980, leading the Dutch's best team in history.

Corey Willis: Led Holland football to its best season as an all-state, dual-threat quarterback before playing receiver at CMU and making NFL practice squad.

Demetrius Lake: This sharp shooter was a three-time all-state honoree and the all-time leading scorer in area history with more than 2,000 career points. He plays professionally in Europe.

Ameer Ismail: All-State football player who became an All-American linebacker at Western Michigan.

Derek Maas: State champion swimmer was an All-American at Alabama before his fifth year at NYU where he won an NCAA championship.

Rob Renes: State champion wrestler was also a starting defensive tackle for Michigan's 1997 national championship football team.

Tabahn Afrik: State champion swimmer went on to compete at Notre Dame, earning All-American honors

Kirk Cousins: Star quarterback started at MSU before a long career in the NFL that resulted in multiple Pro Bowl selections.

Kyle Steigenga: All-state in basketball, football and track, went on to become the all-time collegiate scoring leader in the state of Michigan at Cornerstone.

Mike Mokma: Pitched the Maroons to a state championship before heading to Michigan State and the minor leagues.

Chris Mokma: Was a freshman on the state title team before being drafted and playing multiple years in the minors.

Jim Kaat: A Baseball Hall of Famer, Kaat was a star pitcher at Zeeland High School. He won 283 games in his big-league career and 16 Gold Glove awards before making Cooperstown in 2022.

Jay Riemersma: A multi-sport star, he was a star quarterback in high school before converting to tight end at Michigan, leading to a nine-year NFL career.

Adam Berghorst: A star baseball and football player, he was all-state in both. Drafted by the majors, he opted to play both baseball and football at Michigan State.

Ron Essink: State champion wrestler played football at GVSU then seven years for the Seattle Seahawks in the NFL.

Owen Stevens: Five-time state champion swimmer qualified for junior nationals and now swims at Louisville.

Zach VanValkenburg: All-State wrestler and football player starred at Iowa before signing with the Rams in the NFL.

Jordan VanDort: All-state in football, VanDort graduated as the basketball school-record-holder for points. Led the Dux to a state football title before playing at WMU, GVSU and Hope.

Carson Gulker: An elite basketball player, he made a bigger mark in football where he was all-state before leading Ferris State to multiple NCAA titles. Just transferred to MSU.

Grant Wolfram: Star in basketball and tennis, he was better on the diamond, earning multiple all-state honors before playing at CMU and Davenport. He currently pitches for the Baltimore Orioles.

Kevin Haverdink: Was part of state champion basketball team in 1984, went on to play football at Western Michigan then several years as an offensive lineman in the NFL for the Saints.

Nick Carlson: Won two golf state titles and was runner-up his other two years. Plays professionally overseas.

title: Verstappen is already on holiday, but these drivers remain busy at the Hungaroring
description: While some drivers are already enjoying the summer break away from the track, Formula 1 remains busy at the Hungaroring this week. After the conclusion of the Hungarian Grand Prix, Formula 1's summer break got underway.
fullText:
While some drivers are already enjoying the summer break away from the track, Formula 1 remains busy at the Hungaroring this week.

After the conclusion of the Hungarian Grand Prix, Formula 1's summer break got underway. Max Verstappen, for example, already headed to the beach yesterday while celebrating his partner Kelly Piquet's daughter Penelope's birthday with the family.

However, the Hungaroring remains busy on Tuesday and Wednesday with several test sessions taking place. To begin with, Pirelli is conducting a two-day tyre test. On the opening day, Jak Crawford drove for Aston Martin, Gabriel Bortoleto was in action for Audi, and Franco Colapinto tested for Alpine.

The three drivers did screening runs on the C3 compounds, and the two South Americans also did qualifying simulations and higher-mileage stints on the C4 and C5 compounds as well.

The Pirelli tyre test at the Hungarian Grand Prix continues today with Colapinto and Bortoleto. On social media, the Argentinian wrote: "Testing, so many laps, and so much heat! Tomorrow last day and mini break!"

The updated Honda power unit will make its on-track debut at the Hungaroring today, as GPblog previously reported.

During a Formula 1 filming day, teams are allowed to complete up to 200 kilometres and can hold two such days per season.

Aston Martin introduced 16 updates for the Hungarian Grand Prix. After reaching Q2 for the first time this season, Fernando Alonso has already expressed satisfaction with the team's progress.

He explained to GPblog, among others: "I think it was important. Definitely it was important for everyone in the team, as you know, it has been a tough period in both factories, having the deficit that we had in terms of performance in the first half of the year.

"And this package obviously didn't change many positions but it changed a lot the momentum of everyone in the factory.

"It's not anymore that we are chasing something that we don't know, we know exactly what we are looking for, and we know exactly the targets for the next package or the targets for next year. So that's I think for me the biggest change of this weekend," the Spaniard concluded.

title: Have season ticket holders 'passed their sell-by date' for clubs?
description: BBC Radio Manchester's Gaz Drinkwater and Joe McGrath discussed restrictions on season tickets in the latest episode of The Devils' Advocate.  Manchester United has restricted the accounts of "thousands" of fans, in an operation aimed at identifying potential ticket touts.  Drinkwater said he has "full sympathy" for fans who have fallen under the restrictions despite not being involved as touts.
fullText:
BBC Radio Manchester's Gaz Drinkwater and Joe McGrath discussed restrictions on season tickets in the latest episode of The Devils' Advocate.

Manchester United has restricted the accounts of "thousands" of fans, in an operation aimed at identifying potential ticket touts.

Drinkwater said he has "full sympathy" for fans who have fallen under the restrictions despite not being involved as touts.

"It's pretty obvious that these were fans that were not touting tickets," Drinkwater said.

"I love that Manchester United fans have made such a massive, loud deal about this and football fans have got behind it as well because hopefully that means that these appeals will be listened to."

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire joined the podcast and gave his thoughts on why United might be taking this course of action.

Maguire said: "There's the theoretical one which is perfectly understandable. There's an awful lot of touting at Manchester United as with other big clubs - Liverpool are similar, Arsenal are similar, Chelsea and so on. There's a lot of people making a lot of money through the resale of tickets.

"The other issue is that season ticket holders, to a certain extent, have passed their sell-by date as far as the senior people at the club are concerned. If you're a local Red and you're going 19 times a season to Old Trafford, you're not going to the merchandise 19 times a season.

"You're paying high but not excessive prices for your ticket and those tickets could be repackaged by the club and they could send you to a warehouse in Trafford Park and give you a pie and a pint before the match and get a former player to tell a few anecdotes and they could sell those tickets for £200-£300 a pop. That's what the club wants."

On how the club can manage the situation without upsetting the loyal fans, Maguire said: "There's no easy way around this. Nobody is denying that touting isn't a problem at the club but the way that they have taken [to deal with it] has been quite unpleasant."

title: Cody Bellinger injury adds urgency to Yankees trade deadline plans
description: Cody Bellinger's Grade 2 hamstring strain adds pressure on the Yankees to upgrade before the MLB trade deadline.
fullText:
Cody Bellinger’s worse-than-expected hamstring strain adds a new layer to the Yankees’ trade deadline period.

Diagnosed on Monday with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain, Bellinger’s four-to-six week timeline to return puts him back in the Yankees’ lineup sometime in September.

But even with Bellinger, a compromised Yankees lineup – no Aaron Judge since June 2, no Giancarlo Stanton since April 25 – had become a deeper issue.

Before their 9-5 win against the White Sox on Monday night, the second-place Yankees were 14-19 since June 19, averaging 3.27 runs per game.

Prior to that, the Yankees were averaging 5.27 runs per game and leading the AL East by 3.5 games.

Of course, every pinstriped hope of a deep October run is connected to Judge’s return.

And we’re still waiting on the second re-imaging of Judge’s fractured first right rib, and for his clearance just to begin baseball activity.

With Stanton, the constant he’s-getting-closer narrative should never limit the pursuit of more offense.

Still, impact bats are tough to find in this trade market, and you wonder about the appeal for the Yanks to absorb a bad contract or another DH-only type.

In recent days, potential offensive targets in Cincinnati’s Spencer Steer (wrist), San Francisco’s Casey Schmitt (knee) and even A’s catcher Shea Langeliers (knee), a longshot trade candidate, have receded due to injury.

A right-handed hitting outfielder is a better Yankee fit, and Kansas City has two impending free agents in Starling Marte and Lane Thomas. And the Mets' Tyrone Taylor is an increasingly intriguing option.

Elsewhere, if the Tigers choose to trade lefty ace Tarik Skubal, might they also be inclined to deal fellow impending free agent Gleyber Torres?

But the defensive fit in the Bronx is an issue, which also applies to Padres’ lefty-hitting second baseman Luis Arraez, also in his free agent walk year.

Still, the Bellinger situation doesn’t alter the Yanks’ top areas to upgrade.

The search for a swing-and-miss reliever and a right-handed hitting catcher could take the Yankees right up to Monday’s MLB trade deadline.

With an .856 OPS in nine games since his return from a left hamate bone fracture, right-handed hitting Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers – an impending free agent – is one possible target.

But the Twins are also three games back in the middling AL Central and one game behind for the last AL wild card spot entering Tuesday, so Jeffers’ trade status remains an interesting case.

And if there’s one huge trade to be made this deadline period, San Diego closer Mason Miller is the all-in candidate, with monumental end-game impact and team control through 2029.

If the Padres are inclined, lefty reliever Adrian Morejon – a free agent after this season – is a solid trade candidate. Plus, the Yanks’ past solid relationships with Luke Weaver and the rehabbing Clay Holmes (leg fracture) puts the Mets in play as a potential trade partner.

Bellinger’s absence further weakens the Yankees defensively, an overall area that needs to be addressed.

With appreciation of his utility value, Max Schuemann is an infielder playing out of position in left field, where Bellinger’s 19 defensive runs saved this year has boosted one of the league’s best pitching staffs.

For all his hard work and leadership, Amed Rosario is a liability at any defensive position, and he’s been less of a lefty masher this year, batting .197 overall in his last 25 games.

Top Yankees’ prospect George Lombard Jr. has initially struggled to hit each time he’s moved up a level, and you’d be asking a lot for him to debut in a pennant race.

But his plus-defensive skills at shortstop make him a prime candidate for an August call-up, as one more way to bolster the club’s pitching – its primary strength.

At last year’s deadline, the Yankees became a much better team down the stretch, in part, because of third baseman Ryan McMahon’s defensive presence.

Lombard could have that kind of impact even if he bats .208, which was McMahon’s average in 54 games after his arrival last summer from Colorado.

title: 'Pressure on already' but 'promising signing' - your views on Hogh signing
description: Celtic fans, we asked you for your thoughts on new club-record signing Kasper Hogh.  With so few options, an injury or an underperformance from one of these two signings (although Camilo Duran has looked class so far) has the potential to bring things with the fans to boiling point.  Patrick: Seems like a great signing.
fullText:
Celtic fans, we asked you for your thoughts on new club-record signing Kasper Hogh.

Overall for Bodo/Glimt, the Denmark striker - who has one goal in four caps for his country - has averaged a goal every other game, netting 54 times in 103 matches.

Here is a selection of your views on the club's record addition:

Calum: Promising signing but also a potentially charged one. With so few options, an injury or an underperformance from one of these two signings (although Camilo Duran has looked class so far) has the potential to bring things with the fans to boiling point. A lot is resting on Hogh's shoulders.

Patrick: Seems like a great signing. A proven goalscorer at the top level is what we've needed for a while. Let's hope he hits the ground running and can make up for the loss of Daizen Maeda.

Kel: Great signing. Need three to four more but he and Duran are excellent players and the level of quality we should be signing.

Paul: Optimistic about Hogh. His Bodo/Glimt record is good and the Norwegian league isn't weaker than the SPFL. While we undoubtedly need a stronger squad with defensive cover across the park; a new central defender and full-back cover essential, plus an improvement to Callum McGregor in midfield (great servant and still capable but best days behind him). If Jota and Cameron Carter-Vickers are fully fit that's a huge boost, and CCV will bring much-needed security to the back four, with Alistair Johnson (if we can keep him) and Kieran Tierney if he remains fit.
