title: CBS' '60 minutes' announces new slate of correspondents for upcoming 59th season
description: Two months after a major shakeup, CBS’s “60 Minutes” has hired a lineup of new correspondents and contributors in time for its 59th season, including Ross Douthat, a conservative opinion columnist at ...
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — Two months after a major shakeup, CBS's "60 Minutes" has hired a lineup of new correspondents and contributors in time for its 59th season, including Ross Douthat, a conservative opinion columnist at The New York Times, and Norah O'Donnell, former anchor of "CBS Evening News."

The show's new executive producer, Nick Bilton, announced the news in a staff memo Tuesday, shared on X. Joining Douthat and O'Donnell will be author Sebastian Junger, Trevor Phillips and Gianna Toboni. All will be contributors to the show.

The new journalists join current correspondents Lesley Stahl, Jon Wertheim and Bill Whitaker. Their hirings come two months after a shakeup at the storied program, led by the network's new editor-in-chief, Bari Weiss.

Weiss installed Bilton, who has little substantive broadcast news experience, as executive producer, replacing Tanya Simon, who was let go after a 30-plus year tenure with the show. Also let go were correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega — and soon after, Scott Pelley, after a tense confrontation with his bosses over the changes.

In addition to the three dismissed, Anderson Cooper — whose primary job is at CNN — said earlier this year he was leaving of his own accord after two decades.

Weiss and Tom Cibrowski, the CBS News president, praised the new hires in an internal memo. "We couldn't be more excited about this news," the two said, welcoming the new additions. "Onward!"

Bilton called Douthat "one of the preeminent public intellectuals in America today, a thinker of uncommon rigor and a journalist of deep empathy." The columnist has spent nearly two decades at the Times and is an author of numerous books.

The producer called O'Donnell "a powerhouse."

"You've seen her all over the network. She's launched a new podcast. And you'll see much more of her in our halls because Norah will be a correspondent on 60 Minutes."

Bilton praised Junger for his nonfiction work "The Perfect Storm," about a catastrophic 1991 storm. The book "landed with an electric charge in the world of reported nonfiction, defining an intense and intimate form of storytelling and establishing Sebastian as a generational talent," Bilton said.

Toboni joins"60 Minutes" as a contributor and CBS News as a national correspondent. Previously a senior correspondent with VICE News and VICE on HBO, she comes to the program from CNN.

Calling her a journalist of "extraordinary range," Bilton noted that Toboni has interviewed members of ISIS, investigated cartel violence in Mexico and has written a book on the death penalty.

Also serving as contributor will be Trevor Phillips, announced last month as the news division's senior global affairs correspondent. Based in London, he is "one of the most respected and trusted voices in the United Kingdom for his ability to ask the toughest questions and hold anyone in power to account," Bilton wrote in his memo.

Turmoil had raged at "60 Minutes" for more than a year before the May shakeup. Much of it came after President Donald Trump sued the show over its editing of a 2024 interview with then-Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris.

That became part of a broader shakeup at CBS News after Weiss was named to the new role of editor-in-chief by parent company Paramount late last year following David Ellison's arrival as the network's corporate leader.

Jocelyn Noveck covers the intersection of media and entertainment for The Associated Press.

title: Newly released Biden audio recordings include references to ‘classified’ material and struggles with memory
description: Audio clips released by the right-wing Oversight Project on Monday of former-President Joe Biden’s conversations with his biographer, Mark Lewis Zwonitzer, appears to support what former Special Couns...
fullText:
Audio clips released by the right-wing Oversight Project on Monday of former-President Joe Biden's conversations with his biographer, Mark Lewis Zwonitzer, appears to support what former Special Counsel Robert Hur found in his 2024 report: Biden disclosed classified material, was forgetful and continued to possess classified material after leaving his post as vice president.

In the audio tapes, Biden can be heard cavalierly discussing the notes he kept from his time as vice president as he showed them to Zwonitzer.

"They didn't even know I had this," Biden said while apparently showing the ghostwriter his old notes as reference points in their discussion of allegedly classified foreign policy matters during his VP days. The information is still redacted in the audio clips.

The tapes were released by the Oversight Project, a branch of the conservative think-tank powerhouse Heritage Foundation, who had successfully sued the Justice Department to release them. Biden had fought the release to no avail, ultimately deciding to give up the battle by withdrawing his legal challenges on Monday.

A representative for Biden declined to comment specifically on the release of the audio clips Monday, but spokesperson TJ Ducklo said in a statement last week: "President Biden's conversations for a book a decade ago that discussed his late son are private, and were provided to the Department of Justice on the express condition they stay that way. Reversing course and making them public is just the latest example of this Administration weaponizing the DOJ for political retribution."

In multiple instances in the audio tapes, Biden stumbles in remembering dates and information during the interviews with his ghostwriter, and leaves some thoughts unfinished.

In one instance, while discussing apparently sensitive information that has been blacked out in transcripts of the interviews and muted in audio clips, Biden appears to forget what he was going to ask, adding "oh gosh. I, I can't think of what it is."

When he is seemingly reminded of the subject at hand, Biden warns his ghostwriter, "some of this may be classified, so be careful."

At other times, Biden points to others who might have information about the topic being discussed.

While trying to recall the name of an economic advisor, Biden says, "I should write the names down because I keep forgetting them."

In the Hur report, Biden is described as an elderly man "with a poor memory."

Hur ultimately decided not to bring a case against Biden in part because of his cooperation, which supported the notion that he had not intentionally broken the law but instead did so mistakenly. But Biden's memory and age also weighed into the decision and how a jury might respond to such prosecution.

"Since March 2024, the Oversight Project and the Heritage Foundation fought tooth and nail to bring these tapes to light," the group said in a statement on Monday. "Together, we defeated both the Biden-led Justice Department and his high-price private attorneys. These tapes we are releasing today should have come out a long time ago."

Biden, in one of the released audio clips, said to his ghostwriter that he had "just found" classified documents and then proceeded to lay out his case for why in 2009 he argued against then-President Barack Obama sending troops to Afghanistan.

"So this was – I, early on, in '09 – I just found all of the classified stuff downstairs. I wrote the President a handwritten 40-page memorandum arguing against deploying additional troops to Iraq – I mean, to Afghanistan on the grounds that it wouldn't matter, that the day we left would be like the day before we arrived" Biden said.

In another interview with the ghostwriter, Biden referred to classified information, but the context was unclear.

"And then — and then the next thing I have here is — this is classified," Biden said.

Biden said former President Barack Obama used to really "get pissed" at him over disagreements on how to handle the economy in the aftermath of the 2008 financial crisis.

"I was a really lonely voice on housing, I was a lonely voice on the middle class. I mean, I thought we should be much more aggressive than putting these guys in jail and the bankers," he said. "I mean, he used to really get pissed at me," he added, referring to Obama.

He said the reason the administration did not do more was because Obama and his allies were "subconsciously" beholden to "Silicon Valley."

"I think the reason why we didn't do more, by the way, is because I think that — this is a harsh thing to say — But I think subconsciously, at least, Barack and his guys were beholden to Silicon Valley," he said. "And the valley guys didn't want the shit that I — you know, I wanted," he said.

Biden also said that Obama backed away from a "promise" to appoint Larry Summers to the Federal Reserve because the prominent economist was a "liability."

"He was, you know, Harvard and women," Biden told Zwonitzer. Summers, who once served as Treasury secretary under President Bill Clinton and as president of Harvard University, has caught backlash over his ties to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Biden said that one thing he wasn't focused on while the administration was trying to save the economy was "how rapidly the economy was changing."

"I wasn't focused on robots and artificial intelligence and, and digitalization and Moore's law. I mean, it was all about — and I really believed that, and I still believe it, that we could bring back the manufacturing in America," he said.

The tapes also included a several-minutes-long recollection from Biden of a lunch meeting with Obama, where Biden said the then-president gave him advice about whether he should run for president in 2016.

"He said it's my decision to run or not. It doesn't have to do with the field," Biden recalled.

Biden indicated that Obama questioned whether his vice president could win the nomination over Hillary Clinton, saying that it would "really be an uphill battle," according to Biden.

"The fact is that he didn't think it was doable at that time, that I could, that I could actually go out and get the nomination," Biden said. "That was my read at the time."

It's not clear from the recording when the meeting between Biden and Obama took place, though Biden provided the details to his ghostwriter just days before the 2016 election, on November 3, 2016.

Biden talked to the ghostwriter about various meetings he had with top advisors strategizing about whether he should announce a run for president, how he should frame his candidacy and when he should announce. In the audio recording, Biden does not specify the year the meetings took place.

"Consensus is that it's no longer a question about is the race doable, it is, the question was when would I need to show my hand to be plausible, he said.

In another meeting, Biden recalled one of his advisers telling him, "you have the ability to be a unifier, a reassuring skill. Hillary is divisive and Bernie is too angry."

Biden also discussed with aides what some of his challenges as a candidate would be and one mentioned his gaffes as one of the many obstacles he would have to overcome.

"Gaffe issue, is like a virus. It's dormant, when you make a mistake again they'll bring it up," Biden said, appearing to be reading from his notes.

"I can't read my own writing" the former president said at one point.

This headline and story have been updated with additional details.

title: Video shows Iowa road rage suspect surrender after police order him to drop gun
description: Dramatic video shows the moment Des Moines police confront Bradley Ratkovich after he allegedly pointed a Glock 9 mm handgun at two teenagers.
fullText:
Dramatic video captured the moment Des Moines police confronted an armed road rage suspect after officers said he threatened to shoot the occupants of another vehicle following a minor crash.

Officers responded around 2:30 p.m. Friday after receiving reports that one of the drivers involved in a crash in Des Moines was pointing a handgun at another driver, according to police.

Police identified the suspect as 43-year-old Bradley Ratkovich.

Watch: Driver Smirks In Mugshot After Allegedly Hitting Group Of Cyclists In Caught-on-camera Road Rage

Investigators said evidence, including witness statements and video recordings, indicates Ratkovich got out of his vehicle after the crash and pointed a Glock 9 mm handgun at the 18-year-old driver of the other vehicle and his 16-year-old female passenger. Police said Ratkovich also threatened to "shoot."

Video shared on X by witness Joshua Barzon appears to show Ratkovich standing in front of the occupied sedan while pointing a handgun toward the occupants.

As sirens approach, a Des Moines police cruiser pulls up and an officer immediately exits the passenger side with his weapon drawn.

California Deputies Use Magnet-equipped Drone To Disarm Knife-wielding Sex Offender Hidden In Garage

"Put the gun down," the officer yells.

Ratkovich then places the handgun on the ground.

Follow The Fox True Crime Team On X

"Step back! Get back. Put both hands on top of your head now," the officer continues as a second officer exits the patrol vehicle. The officers then move in and take Ratkovich into custody without incident.

As the confrontation unfolded, Barzon can be heard urging the suspect to back down.

"Don't do it. Relax, bro," Barzon says before later telling the suspect to return to his vehicle.

Like What You're Reading? Click Here For More

Barzon later described the encounter in a post on X.

"Road rage almost turned deadly today in my area of Des Moines," he wrote. "A man pulled a gun on another driver at the same intersection I stop at on my commute from work. Thankfully the cops intervened before it was too late. Be careful out there."

Police said Ratkovich was taken to a local hospital for a medical evaluation before being booked into the Polk County Jail.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

He was charged with two counts of assault while displaying a dangerous weapon, two counts of first-degree harassment and one count of being a person ineligible to carry dangerous weapons.

Court records show Ratkovich pleaded not guilty and waived a preliminary hearing. A judge set his bond at $12,000 cash. He is scheduled to appear in court on Aug. 4, with arraignment set for Sept. 9.

Ratkovich's attorney, Kent Balduchi, disputed investigators' characterization of the incident, telling Fox News Digital his client acted in self-defense after being rear-ended while stopped at an intersection.

According to Balduchi, Ratkovich and his son were injured in the crash, and Ratkovich instructed his son to call police before getting out to exchange information with the other driver.

Balduchi said the other driver became aggressive after admitting he did not have insurance and then attempted to leave the scene. As the vehicle moved toward Ratkovich, his client stepped backward, drew his firearm and ordered the driver to stop because he feared he was about to be struck.

"No shots. No erratic or out of control behavior by Ratkovich," Balduchi said. "Mr. Ratkovich did not display or draw his firearm until he felt endangered. We will file a notice of self-defense."

Balduchi also said the other driver had been cited about three weeks before the incident for allegedly driving without a valid driver's license and liability insurance, adding there was no indication those issues had been resolved before the crash.

The crash investigation remains ongoing as investigators await traffic camera footage, police said.

"Traffic crashes can be stressful, but introducing a firearm into a disagreement dramatically increases the risk of violence," the department said in a statement. "If you're involved in a crash, call 911 for police and medical help if needed, remain at the scene, and allow the responding officers to handle the situation safely."

title: ‘He’s bored’: Banfield has theory on Kohberger plea reversal push
description: "You can't just say, 'I was cheated. I didn't get it.' You can't do that," Banfield said.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — A year after pleading guilty to the murders of four University of Idaho students, Bryan Kohberger is challenging his conviction.

According to a handwritten post-conviction petition, the criminology student claims he was "convinced to falsely confess" to the crimes. He claims he was swayed into the plea deal that landed him life in prison through "coercion, disinformation, false promises, and the withholding of exculpatory discovery."

While Kohberger claims he had ineffective counsel who "misrepresented" what life in prison would be like, NewsNation contributor Ashleigh Banfield told Hena Doba on Monday she believes Kohberger's just bored.

"Life in prison is really awful," she said. "And when you're his age, you're facing about 70 years of this last one year that he's had. He didn't like his last year. He's been in solitary. It's boring. He's tired of it."

Banfield also believes it's not just prison life getting him down, but that Kohberger misses the spotlight he had during his trial.

"He's got a massive ego, and he wants to be relevant again, and he wants to be heard."

As for his claim that his attorneys coerced him into pleading guilty to the murders of Madison Mogen, Xana Kernodle, Ethan Chapin, and Kaylee Goncalves in November 2022 — Banfield doesn't believe that for a second.

"This is a criminology student who was in a Ph.D. program and who intelligently, according to the judge's own words, made them freely and voluntarily in court," Banfield said. "You do have the right to appeal when you think your attorney may have screwed you. The truth is, Anne Taylor could not be a better attorney. She saved that man's life."

Banfield noted that if a judge decides to look into reversing his guilty plea, Kohberger would need a robust argument to prove his attorney was ineffective or withheld evidence that could have proven his innocence.

"You can't just say, 'I was cheated. I didn't get it.' You can't do that," she said. "And I don't believe for an instant that there's some magical discovery that was somehow suppressed from his view."

title: Democratic Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate doesn't recall 'abolish the Senate' post in 2021, campaign says
description: Francesca Hong's campaign said she doesn't recall her 2021 "Abolish the Senate" post and that it's not her current position in a comment to Fox News Digital.
fullText:
Democratic Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong's campaign told Fox News Digital Tuesday that she does not recall posting on social media in favor of abolishing the Senate in 2021 and said that was not her current position.

Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) co-chair Megan Romer went viral Sunday for confirming that the DSA supported abolishing the Senate, eliminating national borders and prisons, replacing the presidency and the Supreme Court, and more during an interview with Shannon Bream on "Fox News Sunday."

Republican candidate for Wisconsin governor Tom Tiffany said in a post to X that Hong believed in all the ideas mentioned in the viral video.

"This sounds a lot like DSA-backed @FrancescaHongWI. Does she want to abolish the police? Yep. Does she want to abolish prisons? Absolutely. Did she call for abolishing the U.S. Senate? Yes. Socialism is knocking on Wisconsin's door. This November, we slam it shut," Tiffany wrote.

Dem Socialist Running For Wisconsin Governor Pushed 'Abolishing The Police'

When reached for comment, Hong's campaign said Tiffany was lying and said she never supported abolishing the Senate.

"Tom Tiffany is once again telling lies and inventing quotes, because he can't run on his record," Hong communications director Allison Geyer told Fox News Digital. "Rep. Hong has never called for abolishing the U.S. Senate. Tiffany cannot produce a single statement where she did, because it doesn't exist."

"She has spoken about police and prison abolition in the past as an aspirational goal, but it is not her current position, and it's not something she will pursue as governor," she continued. "She does not support replacing the presidency with the Supreme Court. Eliminating national borders isn't her position either, and it's not even part of the official DSA platform."

"DSA is a membership organization, not a political party. Rep. Hong is not endorsed by DSA national, and doesn't agree with everything in its national program," Geyer added.

Mamdani-backed Socialist In Hot Seat Again Over Deleted Posts Praising Communism, Marxism: 'Crazypants'

Tiffany's campaign pointed Fox News Digital to a post on social media from February 2021, in which she wrote on X, "Abolish the Senate."

Hong was responding to a post at the time highlighting Congress' vote to acquit President Donald Trump in an impeachment trial on the charge of inciting an insurrection for the Jan. 6 Capitol riot. A majority of senators found Trump guilty in a 57-43 vote, but the number fell 10 short of the supermajority needed to convict the president.

Hong's campaign told Fox News Digital that the gubernatorial candidate did not recall posting it.

Watch: House Dems Dodge Questions On Socialist Agenda That Threatens To Abolish Key Institutions

"The post is from February 13, 2021, the day the Senate acquitted Donald Trump for inciting January 6th," the campaign said. "She quote tweeted an analysis of that vote showing the senators who voted to convict represented roughly 70 percent of the country. It was a frustrated reaction to that day. It is not her current position, and it is not something a governor has any role in. She's running to lower costs, fund public schools, and make childcare affordable."

The campaign said Hong has made her views on the matter very clear in recent interviews. Hong's campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for the specific interviews.

Hong is not endorsed by the national chapter of the DSA, but her campaign website lists the Milwaukee, Northeast Wisconsin and Madison DSA chapters on her endorsement page.

Tiffany told Fox News Digital in a statement on Tuesday, "Democrat Socialist Francesca Hong can flip-flop all she wants, but she can't hide who she is. She's a card-carrying socialist who called to abolish the police, ICE, and even the U.S. Senate. title: Nolan Wells mystery deepens as email indicates teen drank heavily before vanishing
description: A newly released Marine Patrol email listed 18-year-old Nolan Wells’ alcohol intake as “heavy" during the search for him after he disappeared on a boating trip to Horn Island.
fullText:
The mysterious death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells has taken another turn after a newly obtained document listed the missing teen's alcohol intake as "heavy" as authorities searched for him on Horn Island over the Fourth of July weekend.

The document, a July 5 Mississippi Department of Marine Resources Marine Patrol email obtained by Fox News Digital, was sent to the U.S. Coast Guard as authorities searched for Wells.

Along with his physical description and last known location, the email lists "Alcohol intake: Heavy," but does not identify the source of that information.

Wells disappeared while on a boating trip to Horn Island with friends. An extensive multi-agency search ended July 6 when his body was discovered.

Search Called Off After Body Matching Missing Teen Nolan Wells Found Off Mississippi Coast

Authorities have not publicly identified a cause or manner of death, and the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's autopsy and toxicology results remain pending.

The newly reported details come days after a private autopsy commissioned by Wells' family concluded his cause and manner of death were "undetermined pending investigation."

Nolan Wells Independent Autopsy Doesn't Point To Foul Play, Former Medical Examiner Says

During a July 22 news conference, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said an area of "red discoloration" was found on the back of Wells' head but said Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed the independent autopsy, could not determine a cause or manner of death pending further investigation.

"Crime Stories with Nancy Grace" host Nancy Grace later discussed the findings on her show, where she raised additional questions about the investigation.

She pointed to what she described as deep red tissue beneath the skin at the back of Wells' head and said the independent pathologist did not receive Wells' lungs or throat when conducting the second autopsy.

Grace also questioned whether those findings could be significant but emphasized that she did not know what caused Wells' death and noted there were "many accidental possibilities."

"There is deep, red, subcutaneous tissue" on the back of Wells' head, Grace said, adding that the discoloration was localized rather than consistent with postmortem blood pooling.

"I don't know," Grace said. "There are many accidental possibilities."

The Jackson County District Attorney has defended the investigation amid growing public scrutiny, saying authorities are following standard procedures and awaiting forensic testing before drawing conclusions.

Authorities have not announced whether foul play is suspected.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Jackson County Sheriff's Office and the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's Office for comment.

title: Ukrainian foreign minister says he warned Iranian counterpart against escalation, support for Russia
description: July 28 () - Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Tuesday he called his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araqchi, following Iran's ‌denunciation of a Ukrainian drone attack on one of its ‌ships,...
fullText:
July 28 (Reuters) - Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Tuesday he called his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araqchi, following Iran's ‌denunciation of a Ukrainian drone attack on one of its ‌ships, warned him against escalation and told him to end all support for Russia.

"I ​emphasised the necessity to refrain from any escalatory steps, as well as to end any support for Russia's war against Ukraine. This war is illegal and it must end," Sybiha wrote on X of his ‌conversation with Araqchi.

Araqchi confirmed ⁠on X that he had been assured by Sybiha that the attack on the Iranian ship was unintentional ⁠and that Kyiv did not seek escalation.

"Iran does not seek escalation either, but made clear any attack on our citizens or interests is unacceptable. ​There must ​be restitution for losses," Araqchi ​said.

Araqchi had said on Sunday ‌that the Ukrainian attack on the Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, which killed one sailor and injured another, could not go unanswered.

Sybiha said Ukraine's actions were "aimed solely at defending our country from Russian aggression and never intended to target civilian vessels or people".

In more ‌than four years of conflict with ​Russia, Ukraine has faced barrages of Iranian-designed ​drones.

Kyiv has, over that time, ​developed technology to counter drone threats and has ‌offered its assistance to Middle Eastern ​countries facing strikes ​launched this year by Tehran.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar, meanwhile, wrote on X that he had spoken to Sybiha and "discussed the ​challenges facing our nations, ‌including the threat posed by Iran."

He said he looked forward ​to deepening cooperation with Ukraine.

title: Trump asks Supreme Court to throw out E. Jean Carroll's $83 million verdict, Axios reports

fullText:
WASHINGTON, July 28 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump's lawyers are asking the Supreme ‌Court to overturn an $83.3 million defamation ‌judgment he was ordered to pay to writer E. ​Jean Carroll, Axios reported on Tuesday.

The U.S. Justice Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Court records showed earlier ‌this month that ⁠Carroll has collected nearly $5.63 million from Trump. She has won $88.3 million in ⁠civil verdicts against the president in the seven years since he first denied having ​raped her ​around 1996 in ​a Bergdorf Goodman ‌department store dressing room in Manhattan.

Jurors awarded Carroll $5 million based on a 2022 Trump denial, though they did not find that Trump raped her.

A different jury in 2024 ordered ‌Trump to pay Carroll $83.3 ​million, based on his ​original 2019 denial ​during his first White House ‌term.

Trump's latest appeal reported ​by Axios comes ​a month after the justices declined to hear his bid to overturn the $5 ​million verdict ‌that jurors ordered him to pay ​Carroll.

title: Cyclospora outbreak may involve more than lettuce, former CDC lead says
description: Robert Redfield told "Elizabeth Vargas Reports" there's a risk to the public right now with fresh produce and where it's purchased.
fullText:
(NewsNation) — The cyclospora outbreak continues to be a point of concern for health professionals, with one former CDC director saying people should now be cautious about more than just lettuce.

Michigan health officials noted Monday there are 9,253 cases in the state and 160 residents were hospitalized as of last week. The disease has been linked to other states in the Midwest, with a record number of cases being reported.

The CDC has documented more than 4,000 laboratory-confirmed cases, and state records suggest the total number of cases has increased to nearly 12,000.

Recently, a second separate cyclospora outbreak, with no known origin, has sickened 72 people as of last week.

Robert Redfield told "Elizabeth Vargas Reports" there's a risk to the public right now with fresh produce and where it's purchased. He specifically pointed out internationally sourced produce as an issue.

"If you look historically at the outbreaks we've had in the United States, they've really come from produce that was sourced outside of the continental United States," he said.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration linked the first outbreak to distributor Taylor Farms, which sources its lettuce from central Mexico.

Taylor Farms also voluntarily recalled products distributed across 27 states and sold to Taco Bell. Officials have added they believe parsley and cilantro are linked to the outbreak, along with lettuce.

Redfield notes it's a good thing the recalls are occurring.

"I think there have been some serious attempts to stop sourcing from central Mexico right now," he added.

Redfield expanded on the sources of the outbreak, agreeing with Scott Gottlieb, the former commissioner of the FDA, that there's one yet to be identified.

Gottlieb acknowledged he doesn't feel the outbreak is fully under control because there are questions about possible regions besides central Mexico responsible for the issue.

The Hill contributed to this report.

Champions Northampton to open Prem season against Newcastle
description: Prem champions Northampton host Newcastle on the opening weekend of the 2026-27 season, with Exeter at home to Gloucester.
fullText:
Champions Northampton will host Newcastle Red Bulls on the opening day of the 2026-27 Prem rugby season.

Saints beat Exeter to lift the trophy for the second time in three seasons in June and start the new campaign at home on Friday, 25 September.

The Chiefs are also at home for their first game, with Gloucester set to visit Sandy Park on the Saturday.

Elsewhere across the opening weekend, Harlequins are at home to Bath on Friday, Sale host Bristol on Saturday evening and Leicester play Saracens in the only match on Sunday.

The 2026-27 Prem final will be held on Saturday, 19 June 2027 at the Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, with the season to take a series of breaks around international fixtures.

After five rounds in six weeks through September and October, there will be a four-week Prem break through November for the autumn matches of the Nations Championship.

With European competition beginning in December there are four Prem rounds across six weeks until January, before a 10-week league pause again in February and March for the Six Nations.

The new season also begins with promotion and relegation officially scrapped from the division.

While no club has been relegated from the Prem or promoted up from the Champ since Saracens in 2020 and 2021, this has now been formalised as part of a series of changes to English rugby voted through in February, as the league moves towards a franchise-style model.

Prem Rugby Cup pool fixtures announced

Prem relegation scrapped from 2026-27 season

A handful of matches next season will also be staged at major stadiums, as has become customary for some Prem clubs in recent years.

Harlequins play their two annual 'Big Game' fixtures at the Allianz Stadium, starting against Northampton, with a Monday night fixture on 28 December over the festive period.

They return to England's home stadium to play Newcastle in round 15 in May.

Gloucester are hoping to return to Villa Park after playing an inaugural game in Birmingham last season, however the venue is still to be finalised.

If all goes ahead they will again play Leicester in round 12 for the Slater Cup on the weekend of 27 March, while Bristol host the Cherry and Whites at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in a west country derby in round 13 three weeks later.

"There's huge momentum behind the Gallagher Prem heading into the new season, following a third consecutive sold-out final, significant international investment in our clubs, record broadcast audiences and soaring interest from younger fans," said Simon Massie-Taylor, chief executive officer of Prem Rugby.

"And following a landmark agreement to change our operating model earlier this year, we are well on the way with our plans to expand the league by the 2029/30 season," he added.

Exeter v Gloucester (15:05 BST)

title: Jersey's Nowacki makes history with Commonwealth gold
description: Filip Nowacki becomes the most decorated Jersey athlete in Commonwealth Games history after winning gold in the 200m breaststroke.
fullText:
Filip Nowacki has become the most decorated Jersey athlete in Commonwealth Games history after winning gold in the 200m breaststroke.

The 18-year-old, who won 100m breaststroke silver on Saturday, becomes only the second person from the island to win a gold medal.

It comes as the world junior and British senior champion looks to take over the mantle from 50m and 100m world record-holder and former Olympic champion Adam Ramsay-Peaty.

Nowacki, who has beaten some of Ramsay-Peaty's British junior records, finished ahead of the 2016 and 2020 Olympic champion in the 100m breaststroke final.

The Jerseyman also pushed Ramsay-Peaty all the way in the 50m final, finishing fifth behind the Englishman who won bronze.

Nowacki led from start to finish as he opened up a 0.72 second lead after 150m before coming home in a time of 2:07.87, beating Canada's Oliver Dawson into second place with Australia's Zac Stubblety-Cook winning bronze.

Nowacki's success has secured Jersey's first gold since Colin Mallett topped the podium in fullbore shooting in 1990.

But in a winning a gold and silver he has surpassed Mallett's feat in Auckland when he also won fullbore pairs bronze with his father Cliff.

Nowacki wins Jersey's first medal in 36 years

Is struggling Ramsay-Peaty nearing the end?

"It's absolutely unreal," Nowacki told BBC Jersey after the victory.

"People don't understand that you just enter such a heavy flow state during the race, and all of a sudden you finish and you pop back into reality and the crowd comes in."

He added: "It's very special and I owe it to two groups of people.

"My family being my main support and my girlfriend, and also I think the big thing in English swimming is coaches often don't get along between boarding school and club coaches, so the second group of people I put that down to is my coaches."

Nowacki has just left Millfield School and will move to Loughborough to continue his training as he aims towards the 2028 Olympic Games.

He won two world junior titles last year, including the 200m breaststroke, and says he is happy with how he has adapted to the senior environment.

"That jump between junior and senior is huge and it's often overlooked.

"So I'm very pleased to have got my hand on the wall first.

"You don't often see swimmers make that jump straight away, so I'm very fortunate and grateful to have made that jump."

The impact of Nowacki's achievement on his home island of Jersey should not be underestimated.

Competitors representing the Channel Island with a population of about 100,000 had won just four medals before these games.

Nowacki has increased that tally by 50% and become the first-ever swimmer from the island to win a medal.

"There'll be children watching tonight that will want to be like Filip, so it means everything to all of the team here and all of those people watching back home," Jersey's chef de mission Jean Cross told BBC Jersey.

"I think we'll see Filip in LA [for the Olympics], there's so many people talking about Filip here and it's just lovely to be associated with a swimmer of his talent

"He's a true ambassador for Jersey, he's done so well."

Nowacki's victories propel him to one of Jersey's greatest ever sports stars.

The Commonwealth Games is the highest level at which athletes from the island, with a population of about 100,000, can compete under their own flag.

Previous to Colin and Cliff Mallett, Jersey had won just two medals in their own right.

In 1986, bantamweight boxer John Sillitoe won bronze in Edinburgh, while Jersey's first-ever medal was also in the ring when Albert Turmel won welterweight bronze in Perth in 1962.

Islanders have won medals for England - diver Dot Macready won 10m gold in 1934, while more recently Serena Guthrie was part of the England team that won netball gold in 2018.

In 2006, Rebecca Herbert was part of the England hockey team that won bronze, while there were two bronze medals in 2002 for islanders representing England - Elizabeth Cann in badminton and swimmer Simon Militis in the 200m backstroke.

But with Nowacki aged just 18 and already a British senior and world junior champion few would bet against the swimmer going on to become the most decorated Commonwealth Games athlete in Jersey's history.

He is also part of the Team GB set up with an aim firmly on the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.

Jersey has not had an Olympic competitor since Militis went to the 2000 Olympics in Sydney and all island eyes will be on their young hero bringing them more glory.

title: O'Connor bounces back to lead O'Dowda in heptathlon
description: Northern Ireland's Kate O'Connor is three events away from a first Commonwealth Games gold medal as she leads the heptathlon after the opening four events in Glasgow.
fullText:
Northern Ireland's Kate O'Connor is three events away from a first Commonwealth Games gold medal as she leads the heptathlon after the opening four events in Glasgow.

In the absence of Katarina Johnson-Thompson, England's Jade O'Dowda is in second place - 49 points down on O'Connor.

After an evening session which took place as rain hammered Scotstoun Stadium, Australia's Mia Scerri is a distant third while England's Niamh Emerson is in medal contention in fourth place.

The heptathlon concludes on Wednesday with the long jump, javelin and 800m.

O'Connor finished second in Birmingham in 2022 behind Johnson-Thompson - who pulled out on the eve of this edition - but is in a strong position heading into the second day of competition.

The withdrawal of the 33-year-old has opened the door for a first new Commonwealth heptathlon champion in eight years, and O'Connor and O'Dowda are the two leading contenders to top the podium.

O'Connor was third in the 100m hurdles behind Canada's Sienna Macdonald and O'Dowda, but took the overall lead with a 1.82m leap in the high jump ahead of the English athlete.

O'Dowda took the lead off O'Connor after the shot put as the Northern Ireland athlete could only land the fifth-best effort in torrential conditions.

But the 25-year-old rallied to dominate her 200m heat with a time of 24.14 seconds - while O'Dowda ran the second-slowest time - to hold a 49-point margin heading into the final three events.

Johnson-Thompson and Asher-Smith out of Commonwealths

Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games

O'Connor said she had never competed in rain as heavy as the downpour that hit Glasgow on Tuesday evening, and admitted she struggled with the elements in the shot put.

"It just kept slipping out of my hands and when your chalk gets wet, you might as well have dish soap on your hands," world silver medallist O'Connor told BBC Sport.

"I'm gutted with it to be honest and when I talk about it, I feel a bit emotional because I've made it a lot easier for the rest of them to beat me, so I've got to work really hard now."

But O'Connor's performance in the 200m was scintillating, and she mastered the conditions on track to take an overnight lead.

"I went out and I ran really quick in that, I threw the gauntlet down and ran as fast as I could to make it difficult for the rest of the girls," she added.

"If the sun was shining and it was a nice warm day, I would have been gutted with that time because I've been running quick in training.

"But considering it's lashing rain and freezing cold out there and I had 10 minutes to warm up, I am delighted with that performance."

Northern Ireland's Anna McCauley holds sixth place after she won the second heat of the 200m, and is within 39 points of a bronze medal.

Prior to that, McCauley had finished sixth in the hurdles and high jump, and posted the seventh-best distance in the shot put with 12.13m.

title: I turned down Love Island and won silver at the Commonwealth Games
description: Katie Shanahan was offered the chance to appear on the dating show last year - but decided she wanted to inspire a new generation of young swimmers.
fullText:
In another reality, swimmer Katie Shanahan might have been looking for love on her favourite TV show - but instead made a decision that would lead her to a silver medal at the Commonwealth Games.

The 22-year-old told BBC Scotland News she was offered the chance to appear on Love Island last year, the reality dating show where singletons are placed in a Spanish villa.

However Glasgow-born Shanahan turned down the offer of sunshine in Mallorca, choosing instead to focus on her sport at the Tollcross swimming centre.

Last Friday she claimed silver in the 200m breaststroke on the opening night of the Games.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

Despite her sporting success, she says would not be averse to a trip to Casa Amor in the future.

"I'm the biggest Love Island fan ever, I've watched every season", she laughed.

"Last year the producers asked me and Abbie Wood [the English swimmer] if we would be interested in doing it.

"I couldn't go on though, because of focusing on the swimming, but who knows in the future? I was a bit tempted but the swimming had to come first."

Love Island, which concluded its 2026 series earlier this week, has aimed to attract a number of athletes to the programme.

Northern Ireland boxers Jon McConnell and Kaci Rock progressed through initial auditions for the show, but then had to drop out to focus on their sport as the Games drew closer.

A number of lower league and non-league footballers have also appeared on the often controversial dating show over the years.

However Shanahan's decision paid off in the pool, and she was seen fighting back tears after securing silver on Friday night.

Having been inspired by seeing Hannah Miley in action at the 2014 Games, Shanahan told BBC Scotland News she hoped future generations might have be likewise inspired by watching her in the pool this time around.

"I've always said that if I can inspire the next generation of athletes coming through, then my job has been done," she explained.

"I know after 2014 watching Hannah I felt inspired, and it would be nice to think that maybe there's some younger girls watching the 200m backstroke this time, and maybe they'll get into swimming from it."

She joked that the main problem since last Friday was finding the time to get back to various friends and well-wishers sending her messages to congratulate her.

"I'm so grateful for the support, and with it being a home Games it feels like that support has been ramped up a bit, which is so nice to experience."

title: Crawley and Brook help Sunrisers beat Super Giants
description: Leeds Sunrisers end Manchester Super Giants' unbeaten start to the season after chasing down 182 thanks to half-centuries from Mitch Marsh and Zak Crawley while Harry Brook chips in with 42.
fullText:
The Hundred men's competition, Headingley

Manchester Super Giants 181-3 (100 balls): Buttler 63* (33), Klaasen 53 (27); Ellis 2-32

Sunrisers Leeds 186-2 (88 balls): Marsh 63 (26), Crawley 56* (34), Brook 42* (17)

Sunrisers Leeds won by eight wickets

Mitch Marsh was at his destructive best as he bludgeoned 63 to help Sunrisers Leeds end Manchester Super Giants' unbeaten start to The Hundred with an eight-wicket win at Headingley.

The experienced Australia opener crashed six fours and five sixes during a fearless 26-ball knock which provided the impetus for the Sunrisers to chase down 182 for victory.

Marsh was bowled by a yorker from Sonny Baker with the score on 118 but the momentum from his tone-setting innings was continued by England duo Zak Crawley and Harry Brook.

Sunrisers skipper Crawley blitzed an unbeaten 56 off 34 balls to notch only his second half-century of the summer, having lost his Test place earlier this year.

Crawley's average in The Hundred (34.50) so far this summer has been superior to what he has managed in the T20 Blast (23.54) and in first-class cricket (20.54).

The 28-year-old felt "in the zone" and was able to play with "a lot of freedom" as he helped his side pull off the highest successful run chase at Headingley in The Hundred.

"I've spent too much of my career trying to prove to people how I can play. I'm buzzing that I've scored some runs, that's what I get joy out of," Crawley told BBC Test Match Special.

"I'm just thankful I can do that, I'm not too worried about who liked it and who didn't - I know I did and that's what I want to do."

Brook chipped in with 42 not out from 17 balls as he also kickstarted his tournament with an innings bristling with clean ball striking.

The England limited-overs skipper had only managed scores of three and eight in his first two innings but mainly dealt in sixes against the Super Giants.

Brook's six boundaries all cleared the ropes, including the winning runs off Noor Ahmad with 12 balls to spare.

Earlier, England wicketkeeper Jos Buttler continued his impressive start to this year's tournament with an unbeaten 63 off 33 balls which provided the bedrock of the Super Giants' 181-3.

Buttler had made a masterful 90 in the Super Giants' emphatic win over Birmingham Phoenix last weekend and followed it up with his second half-century.

Heinrich Klaasen had chipped with 53 off 27 balls while Aussie seamer Nathan Ellis bagged 2-30 to finish the pick of the Sunrisers' bowlers.

The Sunrisers have won two of their opening matches in The Hundred and join the Super Giants, who stay top on net run-rate, Welsh Fire and MI London on eight points.

Classy Mandhana helps Super Giants beat Sunrisers

The Hundred continues on Wednesday with double-headers in Cardiff and London.

At Sophia Gardens, Welsh Fire's women face Trent Rockets at 11:30 BST before the men's sides meet at 15:00 BST, with both home teams aiming to build on positive starts to the campaign.

Meanwhile, it is derby day at The Oval, MI London's women take on London Spirit at 15:00 BST before the men's fixture gets under way at 18:30 BST, as both sides look to gain early momentum in the race for the knockout stages.

You can follow ball-by-ball commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, BBC Sounds and the BBC Sport website and app.

title: Villa offer glimpse into future despite friendly loss
description: Youngsters Brian Madjo and George Hemmings scored in Aston Villa's defeat to Real Sociedad.
fullText:
This season will see a new version of Aston Villa under Unai Emery.

A 4-2 defeat to Real Sociedad on Tuesday will irritate their perfectionist head coach, but there is plenty of time for him to fine-tune the Europa League holders before the start of the new campaign.

With Brian Madjo, George Hemmings, Modou Cisse all likely to feature in the squad going forward there was still plenty to build on from the encounter against the La Liga side.

The display of teenage striker Madjo was one.

Villa are still awaiting the outcome of their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) as they try to register the England Under-17 international, who joined from Metz for £10m in January and does not turn 18 until January next year.

Under-18s cannot complete international transfers, but Villa have argued Madjo was born in London and should be exempt, despite having three caps for Luxembourg.

Fifa does allow some exemptions for minor players to make moves, including if a 16 or 17-year-old transfers within the European Union - something the UK is no longer part of.

At 6ft 4in, Madjo has already been compared to Belgium's Romelu Lukaku and his leveller to make it 2-2 after 56 minutes was simple enough but showed a predatory instinct.

He was a handful for Sociedad, with strength and power unsettling the visiting defenders and, with Ollie Watkins still on a break following England's World Cup campaign and Tammy Abraham returning from a shoulder issue, Madjo has the chance to impress.

While he cannot play in competitive games for Villa, it leaves the tantalising prospect of the hulking youngster being unleashed in the Premier League in the new year, or earlier if the club get their way.

They are still in the market for a striker - Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson remains a top target - but in Madjo they have someone Emery can refine quietly before his entrance into the spotlight.

There is still work to be done, though, and the Villa boss spent a large part of the first half talking to himself and then the bench, with hands on his hips or arms flailing.

Trying to get Madjo and 19-year-old midfielder Hemmings to listen to instructions appeared difficult with neither player following through on Emery's desire for them to pull wider.

'Don't move' was the second-half instruction to Luka Lynch, which needed repeating several times before the 19-year-old winger stopped and then immediately collected the ball.

While Matty Cash, Tyrone Mings and Emi Buendia started against Sociedad, many of Emery's trusted lieutenants were missing.

Villa's World Cup cohort of Watkins, Ezri Konsa, John McGinn, Victor Lindelof, Emi Martinez and record buy Johan Manzambi did not feature, while France left-back Lucas Digne's move to Paris St-Germain has still to be rubber-stamped.

Only Cisse and Joao Gomes were the new arrivals in action and, even then, centre-back Cisse was signed from LASK last summer before spending the season with the Austrian side.

The departure of Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers, coupled with Amadou Onana's serious knee injury which rules him out until next year, has led to a hectic summer.

It was, at times, a hectic game too on Tuesday with Carlos Soler cancelling out Hemmings' opener, before Orri Oskarsson, Gorka Carrera and Inaki Ruperez netted for the La Liga side.

Winger Alejandro Garnacho was absent at Pallet-Track Bescot Stadium after his loan move from Chelsea last week, but the Argentine winger is expected to travel to Indonesia this week for Villa's tour.

The fact there are players still away - or returning from injury in Boubacar Kamara's case - means bodies are needed.

That also means major outgoings for fringe players like Leon Bailey or Evann Guessand - back in training after the World Cup with the Ivory Cost - are not necessarily expected while Villa are away.

Emery's side play Indonesia All-Stars on Saturday, BG Pathum United next Tuesday, before facing Bayern Munich in Hong Kong on 7 August.

Once Villa return, for the Super Cup against Paris St-Germain in Salzburg on 12 August, then the gears will turn faster.

title: Kick It Out wants tougher sanctions as discrimination hits new high
description: Anti-discrimination body Kick It Out says tougher sanctions are needed to punish discrimination in football, as the number of annual incidents hits a record high.
fullText:
The chief executive of anti-discrimination body Kick It Out says tougher sanctions are needed to punish discrimination in football, as the number of annual incidents hit a record high.

Kick It Out recorded 1,255 incidents of discrimination in the 2025-26 season across all levels of English football - up from 960 in the previous campaign.

Samuel Okafor said racism was "deeply ingrained" in the game, but it was a "reflection of wider society".

His comments came as Kick It Out revealed it had also received 1,744 reports of discrimination for 2025-26, which was a 25% increase on 2024-25.

Racism was the most reported with 792 cases - rising 19% - while homophobia rose by 46% to 203, sexism went up 12% and ableism was up by 20%. Antisemitism climbed 43% to 93 reports and there were 60 incidents of Islamophobia, which was an 88% increase.

Okafor added: "Tougher sanctions are needed, and I believe tougher sanctions will come, hopefully in the next few weeks, where people will face the consequences of their actions."

Regulator proposals 'put diversity on subs' bench' - Kick It Out

Abuse in English football a 'crisis' - Kick It Out

The statistics are not a surprise to Umar Ali, who plays for Route One Rovers - a semi-professional team in Bradford.

During Ramadan last year, he was racially abused by a group of opposition spectators as he was waiting to come on as a substitute.

"It was our first game playing while we were fasting," he said. "So obviously we were hungry that day and I was a bit less patient.

"Then when I was getting ready to come on, one of the fans said I should shave my beard off and that I looked like a paedophile.

"One of them picked up a child who was about six, seven years old, and said 'I bet your wife's the same age as this child'."

Umar described the men as in their sixties.

"It's quite distressing, because they're older than my dad," he added. "They're my grandad's age, and they felt comfortable enough to stand there and make comments like that."

Umar said the assistant referee heard the comments and told the referee, who he claims did not take any action.

The police were eventually contacted and the spectators identified. Umar has not been informed of an outcome.

His manager Mohammed Patel was in the dugout during the match and said - while the opposition coaching staff apologised on behalf of their fans - he felt the officials fell short and should have removed those spectators shouting racist and Islamophobic abuse at his players.

Patel said: "It was a really emotional day for us, because the question we asked ourselves after that game is 'Why is it still happening?' Some of the things that were said were absolutely horrific.

"In my opinion, more needs to be done from the top down. We're actively engaging and working with local FAs to try and navigate this problem, but it absolutely needs to be mandated."

The Northern Counties East Football League fined the opposition club £300 and gave them nine disciplinary points. But Patel says that does not address the real problem.

"We've seen harsher punishments for violent conduct on the pitch or red cards, even administrative mistakes," he added.

"Something as serious as this, we were absolutely not happy with the result."

Patel has been lobbying the Football Association, but has not yet received a response.

He said: "Precedents need to be set, harsher sanctions need to be introduced. This comes from the top down."

The FA said in a statement: "We have introduced tougher sanctions for clubs and individuals, a new behaviour improvement programme, and penalty points accumulation charges in the grassroots game.

"This builds on the steps taken to allow for deductions of league points from clubs that are repeated offenders of serious misconduct."

title: 'Mariah Cleggy' channels Messi to swim to gold before relay team take bronze
description: Para-swimmer Stephen Clegg adds Commonwealth Games gold to his earlier silver to take Scotland's tally to seven.
fullText:
Stephen Clegg's coach thinks he's a bit of a diva. "He likes to call me Mariah Cleggy," the Scottish swimmer said.

And the 30-year-old certainly brought the drama to Tollcross on Tuesday, rampaging his way to an unexpected victory in the Commonwealth Games 50m freestyle S14.

The triumph took the host nation's tally to seven golds - and a total of 14 medals - on day five of the 11-day competition and added to the silver Clegg claimed on the opening night in the 100m version of the event.

Medal 15 came little over two hours later, when the 4 x 200m mixed medley quartet thrashed their way to a scarcely-believable bronze in the final race of the evening.

Matthew Ward, and individual medallists Angharad Evans, Keanna MacInnes and Duncan Scott edged out Canada in a hugely-exciting conclusion.

It means Scotland's most decorated Games athlete Scott becomes that bit more decorated - adding his 15th medal across four Commonwealths - while Evans and MacInnes double their tally within the space of a few days.

Each will race again in finals during Wednesday's final session in the pool with the prospect of an even more successful week in sight.

Bee Gees at bowls as Scotland Para-mixed pairs retain gold

Scotland win three medals in 45 minutes to kick-start Glasgow 2026

All the latest from Scotland at the Games

Clegg's gold in the first race of the night was not at all bad for a man who thought his career might be done earlier this season.

After double Paralympic gold in Paris in 2024, Clegg required surgery to address a growth inside his shoulder. A bit of bone shaving. Nothing hugely serious, he says.

But the physical and mental receipts of that have lingered for the man who grew up in the Borders town of Newcastleton with sister Libby - a double Paralympic champion from 2012 - and older brother James, who was tied fourth in this race.

All three have stargardt macular dystrophy, which affects their vision.

"The gold in Paris was special because it was a really tough journey to get there. But this has been more challenging in some ways," he told BBC Sport Scotland.

"It wasn't necessarily a realistic... I don't know if realistic is the right word but I was prepared to not win gold. But I think I swam beyond myself today."

Clegg added: "My coach said something a bit silly earlier, which was that [footballer] Lionel Messi only shows up for the World Cup, and he meant that my experience allows me to step up for these big moments when all season I've been swimming a bit crap.

"He will hopefully agree that I've done that tonight."

And how. Clegg attacked the second 50m of the race with relish and pulled away from his rivals to post a time of 24.73 seconds, half a second quicker than he has gone all year.

It also upgraded the silver he won in Birmingham over the distance - achieved when he was not only four years younger, but in much better shape physically.

All that was playing through his mind as he stood on the podium, lip trembling and trying hard to keep his shape, as Flower of Scotland played.

"I was really struggling to keep it together," said Clegg, who had missed his sister's wedding amid the preparations for these Games. "Once the anthem started playing, I just started shaking and started to tear up a little bit.

"I'm a very emotional person, but I don't really let them out very often. And for me to show that emotion kind of, I think, speaks louder than words for me.

"Every time I tried to articulate it, I've fallen short of the actual feeling. It's a once-in-a-lifetime experience, and I think nothing in my career can really beat that moment. Even winning gold at Paris."

Scott has experienced that, too, and he needed every bit of his nous and nerve to add to his Games tally here.

The mixed medley is a fascinating event. Eight teams of four. Two men, two women in each. Four separate strokes. Two lengths per swimmer. Beyond that, it's bedlam.

Men race women. Women race men. Leads open up and disappear again in a blur of foam. And the noise, not just from the crowds, but the howling athletes too is quite something to behold.

Ward started the Scots off strongly on his backstroke, finishing his shift with the hosts second. Breaststroke gold medallist Evans plunged in next and maintained that position, despite most other nations choosing men for that leg.

MacInnes was on the butterfly. But two of the fastest male fly swimmers in the world were on either side of her. Australia's Matthew Temple and Joshua Liendo of Canada - twice the size and significantly quicker - scorched predictably past the individual silver medallist like she wasn't there.

It left Scott to take over in sixth place. He might have well have started in the city centre, so far behind was he.

But the 29-year-old made up more than four seconds to touch the wall fractionally ahead of Canada's helpless Ella Jansen and spark wild celebrations around Tollcross and win his first relay medal of the week in his third attempt.

"It felt especially special," Scott told BBC Sport Scotland. "I've had a couple of frustrating relays and maybe not delivered quite how I might have wanted for the boys, but that is a nice way to lead us all into the last day."

title: West Indies beat Pakistan & dedicate win to Sobers
description: Jayden Seales takes 5-20 in second innings as West Indies' pace attack ruthlessly blow away Pakistan to secure a 90-run victory just after tea on day four of the first Test.
fullText:
First Test, Tarouba (day four of five)

West Indies 311 (Hope 92; Ali 4-50) & 181 (Joseph 38; Abbas 5-22)

Pakistan 282 (Masood 109; Greaves 5-27) & 120 (Azam 58*; Seales 5-20)

West Indies won by 90 runs; lead series 1-0

Jayden Seales claimed 5-20 as the West Indies pace attack ruthlessly crushed Pakistan to clinch a 90-run victory just after tea on day four of the first Test.

Set 211 for victory, Pakistan were reduced to 71-9 in their second innings on a deteriorating pitch and had looked on course to be bowled out for their lowest total in Tests against the hosts.

However, a battling 10th-wicket partnership between Babar Azam and Muhammad Abbas worth 49 runs took the match into the evening session.

The Pakistan skipper made an unbeaten 58, before Seales secured the success at the Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Trinidad when he had Abbas trapped lbw for 23.

West Indies skipper Roston Chase dedicated the victory to the late Sir Garfield Sobers, who died recently and would have turned 90 on the day they wrapped up victory.

"We wanted to make him proud and had a chat about it before the match. I hope he is smiling down on us," said Chase.

"I also want to thank the Trinidad crowd for coming out and supporting us. It was not a big crowd but it gave us enough energy and support to go out there and perform."

Having resumed on 126-7, West Indies managed to add 55 runs for their last three wickets in the morning session.

Shamar Joseph top-scored for the hosts with 38 off 27 balls, including four sixes, while Kemar Roach made a dogged 18 off 63 balls.

Abbas was the pick of the Pakistan bowlers as he claimed 5-22.

Their chase started to unravel before lunch when Seales removed Imam-ul-Haq, Azan Awais and Salman Agha.

Justin Greaves, who had taken five wickets for no runs on day three during an incredible spell of five wicket maidens, bowled Mohammad Rizwan before he trapped Aamer Jamal lbw as West Indies tightened their grip.

Shan Masood batted with a fractured finger and briefly delayed the inevitable before he spooned a catch to backward point as Pakistan's resistance faded.

Babar was defiant in his knock, but ultimately ran out of partners as his side slumped to their eighth consecutive defeat in Tests away from home.

He said: "We played good cricket in the last few days but today we were not up to the mark as a batting unit.

"There was uneven bounce in the pitch but we should have looked to build partnerships. The basics stay the same, you have to survive the new ball and look to score when it gets a bit old."

Pakistan will attempt to level the two-match series in the second Test in Port of Spain, which begins on 2 August.

title: Despair to delight for Wales' golden girl Evans
description: Gymnast Ruby Evans goes from despair to gold in Glasgow after glory in the floor final at the Commonwealth Games.
fullText:
What a week it has been for Wales' gymnastics golden girl Ruby Evans.

The 19-year-old left Glasgow International Arena in tears on Sunday evening following the disappointment of the individual all-around competition.

Evans finished sixth. She and many others expected more.

Fast forward two days and there were tears of joy as she dazzled to become Wales' first winner of these Commonwealth Games with victory in the floor final.

It has been quite the couple of years for the Cardiff gymnast. This will have been close to the pinnacle.

She delivered when it mattered and under intense pressure, just days after one of her lowest moments, to create history by becoming the first Welsh woman to win an artistic gymnastics Commonwealth Games gold.

Wales at the Commonwealth Games

Team Wales captain Breen claims sprint silver

It has been a 14-year journey to this point.

Evans started gymnastics at the age of five at her local leisure centre in Cardiff with her parents wanting to utilise her energy.

"She used to somersault off the window sills," said mother Leanne, while father Chris admitted they "still did not know anything about gymnastics".

Evans was part of the British team that finished fourth at the Paris Olympics in 2024 - and was the youngest member of the Team GB squad at 17.

In 2025, she won a silver medal on the floor at the World Championships in Jakarta.

As well as her sporting success, she is also popular on social media with more than 117,000 Instagram followers.

So Evans was one of the most recognisable faces in the Team Wales squad coming to Glasgow and under pressure to deliver success, although she was not comfortable with the poster girl image.

"I struggled a bit in camp," admitted Evans. "It was like, 'Ruby Evans, Ruby Evans', so I knew there was a bit of pressure on me.

"You have to block it out as best as you can. I think I did do that."

It has been quite a week for Evans and Welsh gymnastics in general with drama, disappointment and delight in equal measures.

She was part of the Wales women's team that just missed out on a medal in the team event.

The quintet had been part of the second rotation and led the competition before the final four teams performed.

The television cameras kept panning to the Wales team in the crowd, who could only sit and wait to see if they had won a medal, before they were denied a bronze by England.

Then Evans, alongside Emily Roper, went for individual all-around glory.

She was second after two of the four disciplines before she had a terrible beam routine, which included a faltering start and falling off halfway.

That dropped her to seventh and only a miracle on the floor would see her rise back to the top three.

Evans ended up sixth. It left her distraught and you hoped that would not be the defining image of her Games.

She pulled out of the uneven bars on Monday as she rested a shoulder injury.

"I just watched the competition, had some food and chilled and watched the Love Island final," said Evans.

She watched the 20-year-old Roper identical twins provide one of Wales' stories of Glasgow so far in winning bronze medals within a couple of hours of each other.

Abigail beat Emily to the the third podium position in the vault. Emily brushed aside the disappointment of finishing fourth to return to claim bronze in the uneven bars, with the iconic image of her sister cheering her from the stands.

A first Welsh women's vault for 32 years, a first bars medal in history. And immense exposure for the 20-year-old twins they never expected, with numerous interview requests for them and their parents from around the world.

The focus switched to Evans on the final day of competition with two chances of medals.

The watching Wales supporters included chef de mission Gethin Jones and Team Wales captain Olivia Breen, the Para-sprinter who won silver on Monday night.

First it was the beam. The nemesis from the all-around individual final.

Evans came out to a big roar and produced the trademark dragons symbol of the Welsh team before bursting out laughing. She seemed relaxed. A welcome sign.

It was a much more solid performance as she finished seventh. An expected result.

This was just the warm-up before the main event an hour later when the floor competition began.

The word had come that the outfit would not be just the traditional red, white and green of Wales but something sparkly and it did not disappoint.

Evans was the final one of the eight competitors to perform. Would it be a case of saving the best until last?

England's Abigail Martin was first and set the standard. Six others tried and failed to topple her.

Then it was the turn of Evans as her golden costume almost blended into the floor.

There was a hush as she delivered one of the most impressive performances of her short, but glittering, career so far.

Evans stated how she used anger as motivation in her signature discipline. It worked.

"I feel like I perform better when I have a bit of fire in me," she said.

"It's like a completely different feeling. I went out there like my dragon was absolutely firing."

But was it enough? Nobody was quite sure. The Roper twins were pictured on the big screen cheering. They, like everybody in the Welsh pockets of the stands, hoped so.

The wait was agonising. Finally the verdict was in. Wales had its first gold medal.

Evans could not quite believe it.

The round of interviews soon followed, then came the national anthem Wales had been waiting five days of competition for.

The Welsh gymnastics fraternity were still in the building and you could hear their whooping and cheering as Ruby showed off her medal.

Evans was rushed off to Team Wales house to celebrate with family and friends. Playing tenpin bowling there was on the agenda for celebration plans.

"I feel relieved it's done," she added. "I can just chill out and know I did something.

"It's a good feeling and I feel so calm. I'm so chill. My feelings have been everywhere for the past two weeks.

"Now I can just feel nothing. I'm just happy to feel nothing."

What a week for Ruby Evans. One she will never forget.

title: Savinho open to leaving Man City amid Spurs interest
description: Manchester City winger Savinho is open to leaving the club and is keen to join Premier League rivals Tottenham.
fullText:
Manchester City winger Savinho is open to leaving the club with a view to exploring a move to Tottenham.

The Brazil international is a key target for Spurs head coach Roberto de Zerbi and City are aware of the interest in the 22-year-old.

It is understood Savinho is keen to leave during this transfer window, with the machinations towards his potential move to London now under way.

The attacker joined City from sister club Troyes for £30.8m in July 2024, having spent the previous season on loan at Spanish side Girona.

Tottenham held talks to sign Savinho last summer, but the Etihad club were not looking to sell at that stage.

He subsequently signed a two-year contract extension last October, keeping him at City until 2031.

Savinho was a regular under Pep Guardiola in his first season, scoring three times in 48 appearances all competitions.

However, his game time was more limited last term, appearing in 36 matches across all competitions in Guardiola's final campaign as boss.

Savinho had competition for a starting spot with Rayan Cherki, who joined from Lyon last summer, and Antoine Semenyo, a January signing from Bournemouth, also used on the right-hand side.

title: Are there already worrying signs for Vrancken's Hearts?
description: Former Hearts forward Ryan Stevenson delivers a scathing verdict as Wouter Vrancken's reign begins with a chastening Champions League elimination.
fullText:
Former Hearts forward Ryan Stevenson was vociferous in his criticism after Hearts crashed out of the Champions League qualifiers following a 6-0 aggregate hammering from Sturm Graz.

Hearts, who just 73 days prior came within minutes of a historic title win at Celtic Park, have lost their talisman, central-midfield enforcer and manager this summer and now lack a connection between players and fans, according to Stevenson.

"Worrying", "freefall" and "rude awakening" were all bandied around in the immediate aftermath of the club's heaviest ever two-legged European defeat as new boss Wouter Vrankcen's tenure got off to a rocky start.

After the departures of Lawrence Shankland, Cammy Devlin and Derek McInnes to Rangers, and a glut of other players leaving, the club have made 11 new additions and looked disjointed in both legs against their Austrian opponents.

"Hearts just look as if it's just a new squad flung in together, with the manager too, trying to find their way," Stevenson said.

"You don't get time in football, it's game after game after game.

"If you don't get results, we all know what Tynecastle is like. It can be electric, but can they deal with the stadium turning? Are they big enough characters to deal with that?

"If they don't play well, I would give it to mid-September, and it would not be nice."

Outclassed Hearts exit Champions League to Sturm Graz

Hearts sign Mendy for potential Forest Green record fee

Devlin opens up on 'too stressful' Hearts exit for Rangers

Despite conceding six goals across two legs, Hearts impressed going forward in spells but lacked a clinical touch in front of goal, failing to score from a combined expected goals value of 2.6.

With only a couple of competitive games under their belt, there was a sense of unease around Tynecastle, where many fans left well before the final whistle.

The defeat was Hearts' first at home in 15 months and supporters can be forgiven for expecting more from a side assembled with the aid of lauded recruitment tool Jamestown Analytics.

Regardless, it is still just two games into the season for a new-look team who will be expecting to compete for domestic honours and still have a chance at Europa League or Conference League football.

"It's early days, but if you look at that squad, you have to be a big character to go out when things aren't going well to demand the ball and drag the team forward," Stevenson added.

"How long does the manager get if they come under pressure? What do Jamestown do? Do they stick their heels in? And then it becomes ugly.

"It's like an absolute freefall, it's totally a new team. There isn't a connection between the team and the fans. Again, it's the first game, so I'm being totally critical, but the signs for me just now are worrying."

With no competitive warm-ups before their Champions League journey began, Vrancken insists his players weren't ready.

However, in the first leg, nine of the starters were at the club last season. And in Tuesday night's second leg, eight starting players remained from last season.

They looked like strangers at times, particularly in the final third and when high balls were launched into their box.

"Physically, yes," Vrancken said when asked if these games came too soon.

"When you see both games again, what we did with the ball was really good until the moment that you physically cannot bring it any more and that made it difficult.

"I hope everybody starts scoring. It doesn't matter who, as long as the goals come.

"It comes together with physical preparation too, then you make the better decisions, and in the final moments you're there to finish it. I cannot blame the players in intentions and how they did it at all.

"It's not about quality. When you play against Sturm Graz who are experienced in Europe, and you play like that in the first half in both games, then it's not about lacking quality, it's more about we have to make some steps physically."

Hearts' Scottish Premiership duties start on Saturday evening with a tricky trip to Aberdeen, where they have a dismal record, losing 10 of their past 11 league visits.

Their title bid last year garnered worldwide acclaim, but building on that benchmark is a tough ask.

Setting the tone for the season ahead, particularly after such a lacklustre start, is vital, with a performance now just as important as the result.

"It will be an eye-opener for the new players against Aberdeen at Pittodrie," Stevenson said.

"They will be in their faces. It will be a rude awakening. I don't think the fans will accept finishing below third, and I don't know if that Hearts team would finish third.

"I am genuinely worried about Saturday. If you are Aberdeen, you're going to play it off the full-backs, get at them through the middle, and they will steamroll Hearts. They look so weak."

Vrancken, though, struck a more optimistic tone in the face of early turmoil.

"We have to go step by step again, but we can't wait until we're physically top to start getting results," the Belgian said.

"We have to take the results and go into games like we did today, but hopefully finish it."

Scott: We can't defend and we can't score. Players are surely needing time to adjust to the new style of play. It could be a long season ahead but we cannot expect 10 new players to assimilate immediately. We cannot lose a manager and our main striker and expect to carry on from where last season left off. It's hard but we need to face reality.

Ian: Oh dear! The head coach thought we controlled the first half. That worries me if he truly believes that. Third place is the least I expected this season, but, albeit only after two competitive games, we'll get nowhere near that. Poor defensively, overrun in midfield and no goal threat up front is a recipe for disaster.

Chris: The manager has only been in place for a few weeks, but I am already concerned with what I've seen. He said after the game there was a lot of intensity and an energy to score goals, I have to disagree. We looked flustered, disorganised, can't defend and can't score. I'm convinced that we will start the domestic campaign with a defeat if we continue to play in this manner.

Calum: Vrancken's been dealt a bad hand with little time for preparation and a squad and fanbase clearly mentally shattered off the end of last season. That said, the Sturm Graz passing, movement and conviction was night and day. We need to improve fundamentally on Saturday - at a ground we've not won at for 10 or so years!

Graham: No midfield structure, shambolic defence and a blunt attacking frontline. The new manager needs to work out the shape of the team and the players he wants in the side and he needs to do it soon. Shades of Neil Critchley...
